QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the procedure that matches your spindle type and whether a nose cap mounting ring is already installed.

For R-8 spindle taper (machines manufactured on/after Jan 1, 1983; retrofit instructions for earlier machines):
- Place mounting ring “B” underneath the top of guard “D”.
- Insert the two socket head cap screws “A” through the ring and hand-start them into the threaded holes in the spindle nose cap; align guard square to the table (or at desired angle).
- Tighten the screws with a 3/16" Allen wrench.
- If your machine was built before Jan 1, 1983, first tap the existing spanner-wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap (do not drill or deepen holes). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

For Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick-change spindles (attachments made after Jan 1, 1985):
- If nose cap mounting ring has NOT been installed:
  1. Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button-head black finish screw (left of the cadmium-finished screw) and unscrew the locknut counterclockwise.
  2. Place nose cap mounting ring “O” against quill nose cap and install the four button-head cap screws “M” (counterbored side of ring fits against nose cap).
  3. Lower the quill. Place clamping ring “P” underneath the top of guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.
  4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread into the clamping ring.
  5. Align the guard front parallel to the table and tighten the clamping screws.
  6. Reinstall the quick-change locknut (refer to assembly instructions).
- If the nose cap mounting ring HAS been installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6; follow steps 3–5.  
- Note: For Universal #200 quick-change spindles do not remove the quick-change locknut; follow steps 2–5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Attachment location: the guard fastens to the spindle nose cap using the provided mounting ring(s) and socket/button-head cap screws into the threaded holes in the nose cap (or into the clamping ring assembly for quick-change spindles). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf] [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the lubrication schedule for the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Lubrication requirements and schedule (summary from the lubrication chart): [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Way surfaces and lead screws: Sunoco Waylube #1180 (or equivalent). Suggested quantity: a few drops twice daily. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Milling heads (spindle bearings): S.A.E. 10 or 10W light oil (none on grease‑packed heads). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Motor: none required (motor greased for life of bearings). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Grease areas: grease with [unspecified grease] every six months as described on the lubrication plate. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Power feed: fill to sight level with Mobilube No. 46 S.A.E. 140. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Shaping attachment: Mobil 600W oil (or equivalent). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

If you need exact grease type/grease points or the full lubrication plate details, those are referenced on the machine’s lubrication instruction plate (see same file). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: I am boring a hole to accept a press fit bearing with the mill. How can I make sure the bearing can easily go in and stay in place?
STUDENT ANSWER: Bore to the finished diameter using the radial boring canned cycle (for example G245) and use a proper finishing tool with correct tool nose compensation and wear offsets so the hole is the intended final size for the press fit. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf] [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf]

Supporting steps:
- Program the bore with a radial boring canned cycle (G245) to the target X (diameter) and Z (bottom) values and use finishing feed/RPM appropriate for the cutter. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]
- Set the tool nose radius and clear the corresponding Tool Nose Wear Offset to zero when installing a new insert; use a finishing insert and adjust the radius wear offset during setup runs as needed. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Do not operate until you have read and understood the operator and safety/maintenance manuals and all machine/control key signs; receive qualified instruction for first-time use; and verify proper maintenance has been performed and the machine is in good working order. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Pre-operational safety check (recommended steps):
- Verify warning/instruction tags are present and readable. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Put on required PPE: approved safety glasses with side shields and safety shoes; don’t wear gloves, long sleeves, loose jewelry, or unsecured long hair. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Remove any loose parts or tools from the machine and work area (including removing chuck wrenches). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Inspect for unusual or excessive heat, noise, smoke, or vibration and report any problems; do not operate if present. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Ensure point-of-operation safeguarding (chip/coolant shield or other guards) is installed and appropriate for the operation. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Securely clamp and locate the workpiece; verify clamps are clear of the cutter path and use stop blocks if needed. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Confirm correct tooling (not worn/defective), correct spindle rotation for the tool, and proper spindle speed/table feed for the job. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Additional brief notes:
- Always stop the spindle completely before changing tools, loading/unloading workpieces, taking measurements, or opening safeguards. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Be aware that some coolants may damage the polycarbonate safety shield (mono/di/tri-ethanolamine); using such coolants can void the shield warranty. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: If your machine has an Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick-change spindle (manufactured after Jan 1, 1985):

- The manufacturer drilled and tapped four #8-32 holes in the nose cap for mounting the guard.  
- If the nose cap mounting ring has NOT been installed:
  1. Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button‑head black finish screw (normally left of the cadmium screw) and unscrew the locknut counter‑clockwise.  
  2. Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (counterbored side of the ring fits against the nose cap).  
  3. Lower the quill; place clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.  
  4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.  
  5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the clamping screws.  
  6. Reinstall the quick change locknut (refer to assembly instructions).  
- If the nose cap mounting ring HAS been installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6; follow steps 3–5. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

If your spindle is a Universal #200 quick-change, do NOT remove the quick‑change locknut — install the safeguard by following steps 2, 3, 4 and 5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

If your machine has an R‑8 spindle taper (manufactured on/after Jan 1, 1983):

1. Place mounting ring “B” underneath the top of guard “D”.  
2. Place two socket head cap screws “A” through the holes in the ring and hand‑start into the threaded holes in the nose cap until hand tight.  
3. Align the guard square with the table (or at desired angle).  
4. Tighten screws with a 3/16" Allen wrench.  
- If your machine was manufactured before Jan 1, 1983, manually tap the existing spanner‑wrench holes with a .250"-20 bottoming tap (do NOT drill new holes or deepen existing holes). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Where to attach the guard:
- For Erickson #30 / Universal #200: attach to the nose cap via the nose cap mounting ring and clamping ring using the #8‑32 and #10‑32 hardware shown. The guard clamps to the spindle nose cap and is aligned parallel to the front of the table. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]  
- For R‑8 spindle taper: attach the mounting ring to the threaded holes in the spindle nose cap and secure the guard to that ring. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Follow the illustrated parts and hardware lists in the spindle-guard assembly for correct screws and ring items. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the lubrication schedule for the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Waylube the machine ways a few drops twice daily; follow the lubrication table and periodic tasks below. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

Key items from the lubrication instructions (Chapter 1):
- Way surfaces and lead screws: Sunoco Waylube #1180 (or equivalent). — Few drops twice daily. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Milling heads (spindle bearings): SAE 10 or 10W light oil (none on grease‑packed heads). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Motor: none required (motor greased for life of bearings). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Grease (unspecified components): lubricate every six months as described on the lubrication plate. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Power feed oil: fill to sight level with Mobilube No. 46 (SAE 140). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Shaping attachment gear oil: Mobil 600W (or equivalent). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

Additional E‑head gear case schedule (Chapter 3):
- Change gear case oil after the first two months of service, then twice yearly thereafter. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

Do not operate the machine until it is properly lubricated. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: When you select Low (back gear) the spindle rotation is reversed unless you also reverse the motor direction and follow the correct change procedure; if the spindle is running backwards the feed/power feed will not behave as expected. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Key points and correct procedure:
- The High‑Low Range switch is a motor reversing switch; in Back Gear (LOW) the spindle will run counter‑clockwise unless the motor direction is reversed by moving the switch to “Low.” Ensure the Hi‑Lo lever and the switch are positioned alike. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Do NOT change range while the spindle is running. Stop the spindle (Switch B to OFF), move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to LOW, then switch to LOW. If the gears don’t mesh, do not force the lever. [005__L1__Table_of_Contents__pp13-16_part01.pdf] [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

If you followed these steps and still have issues, the provided documents do not give further troubleshooting details.

force the lever

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: I have unplugged the machine so I change the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever on the bridgeport mill. What is the next step I should take?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: You can pull it in toward the machine and change the direction. You will hear the lever click into place.
STUDENT ANSWER: You must manually rotate the spindle by hand to mesh the clutch/gears, then when power is restored set the range switch (drum switch) to the desired range (LOW or HIGH) per the operational procedure. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Supporting details:
- The Hi-Neutral-Lo lever procedures require the spindle be rotated by hand to facilitate meshing of clutch or gears. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- To change range to LOW or HIGH the procedure shows stopping spindle rotation, moving the lever through neutral to LOW/HIGH, and then selecting the corresponding range on the drum switch. (Back Gear: switch to OFF, move lever to LOW, then switch to LOW; Direct Drive: switch to OFF, move lever to HIGH, rotate spindle by hand until clutches engage, then switch to HIGH.) [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I have started the machine so I can change the hi-lo lever on the bridgeport mill. What are the next steps I should take?
STUDENT ANSWER: You must stop spindle rotation, shift the lever through neutral, then restart in the desired range. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Recommended steps:
- Switch the drum/motor switch to OFF to stop spindle rotation. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral into the desired position (Lo for back gear or Hi for direct drive). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- For Lo (back gear) set the drum switch to LOW; for Hi (direct drive) rotate the spindle by hand until clutches engage, then set the drum switch to HIGH. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Cautions:
- Do not shift the Hi‑Lo lever while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- The spindle should run clockwise in normal operation. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to change the depth through knob "I" on the left side of the spindle. How deep should I go if I am boring a 1 inch hole with the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Knob “I” is the Feed Control Lever (it engages the feed/overload clutch), not the depth control; set the boring depth using the micrometer nut and quill stop. The boring depth for a 1.00" hole is 1.00" (set the quill to feed down 1.00"). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Supporting details:
- Use Micrometer Nut “F” with the Quill Stop Knob “E” to set depths; each micrometer graduation = 0.001". [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Quill travel is 5" (so a 1.00" depth is within travel). [010__L1__Chapter_5_-_Specifications__pp115-134.pdf]
- Caution: do not engage power/quill feed above 3000 RPM. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).

- To select Direct Drive (High): switch the drum switch to OFF, move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to HIGH, rotate the spindle by hand until the clutches engage, then set the drum switch to HIGH. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

- Move each unit to the opposite limit stop and clean/lubricate; repeat a third time.  
- Loosen bolts to unlock the ram and move it fully forward and backward to clean and lubricate the ram ways. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

Cautions/limits:
- Do not engage quill feed over 3000 RPM. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the procedure for your spindle type and machine manufacture date.

For machines with R-8 spindle taper (manufacturer drilled/tapped two nose-cap holes; machines built on/after Jan 1, 1983):
- Place mounting ring “B” underneath the top of guard “D”.
- Insert the two socket head cap screws “A” through the holes in the ring and hand-start them into the threaded holes in the spindle nose cap until hand tight.
- Align the guard square with the machine table (or mount at desired angle).
- Tighten the screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

For retrofits on R-8 spindles (machines manufactured prior to Jan 1, 1983):
- Manually tap the existing spanner-wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap (do NOT drill new holes or deepen existing holes).
- Then mount the guard as above. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

For machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick-change spindles (manufactured after Jan 1, 1985) where the nose-cap mounting ring has NOT been installed:
1. Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button-head black-finish screw (normally left of the cadmium-finish button-head screw) and unscrew the locknut counter-clockwise. (Omit this if the nose-cap mounting ring is already installed.)  
2. Place nose cap mounting ring “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button-head cap screws “M”. (Counterbored side of the mounting ring fits against the nose cap.)  
3. Lower the quill. Place clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.  
4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.  
5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws clamping the guard in position.  
6. Reinstall the quick-change locknut (refer to assembly instructions).  
If the nose cap mounting ring is already installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

For Universal #200 quick-change spindles specifically: do not remove the quick-change locknut; follow steps 2–5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Where to attach: the guard mounts to the spindle nose cap using the provided mounting ring(s) and socket/button-head cap screws into the tapped holes in the spindle nose cap (R-8: two tapped holes; Erickson/Universal quick-change: four #8-32 tapped holes in nose cap for the guard). Align the guard with the front of the table when tightening. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf] [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the lubrication schedule for the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Lubricate the machine before operating and follow the lubrication chart in Chapter 1: 
- Way surfaces and lead screws: Sunoco Waylube #1180 or equivalent. 
- Milling heads (spindle bearings): SAE 10 or 10W light oil (none on grease‑packed heads). 
- Motor: none required (motor greased for life of bearings). 
- Grease (item 4 on plate): grease every six months as described on lubrication plate. 
- Power feed oil: fill to sight level with Mobilube No. 46 SAE 140. 
- Shaping attachment: Mobil 600W oil or equivalent. 
Also apply “few drops twice daily” to the areas indicated on the lubrication instruction plate. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided documents do not contain a labeled “pre-operational safety check” procedure for the Bridgeport/M‑450 mill. However, the safety recommendations list specific pre‑use checks and precautions you must observe before operating the machine: 

- Do not operate the equipment until you have read and understood the operator and safety maintenance manuals and all machine and control key signs. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]  
- Do not operate the equipment for the first time without a qualified instructor and do not allow untrained personnel to operate or repair the equipment. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]  
- Ensure proper maintenance has been regularly performed and the equipment is in good working order. Report any unusual or excessive heat, noise, smoke, or vibration, and do not operate if such conditions exist. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]  
- Remove loose parts or tools from the machine and work area; remove chuck wrenches before starting the machine. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]  
- Wear required PPE: safety glasses with side shields and safety shoes; when necessary use respirator, helmet, and hearing protection. Do not wear gloves, long sleeves, long hair, rings, watches, neckties, or jewelry while operating. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]  
- Safeguard the cutting zone (point of operation); use the provided chip/coolant shield and additional/alternate safeguards if required. Verify shields are compatible with coolants (polycarbonate shields are damaged by ethanolamines). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]  
- Stop the spindle completely before changing tools, loading/unloading workpieces, taking measurements, opening safeguards/covers, or changing/adjusting belts, pulleys, or gears. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]  
- Do not remove chips with hands; use a hook or similar device and ensure all machine movements have ceased. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]  
- Securely clamp and locate workpieces; remove flammable materials from the work area and be aware some materials (e.g., magnesium) are highly flammable in chip form. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: How should I clean the bridgeport mill when I first receive it?
STUDENT ANSWER: Thoroughly clean the protective coating from the machine with a suitable cleaning solution; do not use gasoline or any other flammable cleaning agent. After initial cleaning, do not move the table, saddle, knee, or any movable part until all ways have been well cleaned and lubricated. Then:

- Move table, saddle and knee in one direction by hand to the limit stop and clean/lubricate exposed ways.  
- Move each unit to the opposite limit stop, clean and lubricate exposed ways; repeat moving to the opposite stop once more and clean/lubricate.  
- Loosen bolts to unlock the ram and move it forward and backward full length to clean and lubricate.

Also follow the lubrication recommendations (use appropriate way oil and head/spindle oils) before operating. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I set the maximum depth for the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The maximum depth of cut (knee travel / quill travel / spindle-to-table limits) is specified in the machine specifications: quill travel 5" (127 mm), knee (Z-axis) travel 16" (406 mm), ram travel 12" (305 mm), and spindle-to-table range 2.25" (57 mm) minimum to 18.75" (476 mm) maximum. Use these values to determine the maximum workable depth for a given setup. [010__L1__Chapter_5_-_Specifications__pp115-134.pdf]

If you meant setting the automatic quill stop (to limit quill travel) or the micrometer depth stop: set the micrometer nut to the required depth (each graduation = .001") and use the quill stop knob to disengage/stop the automatic feed at that setting; engage auto quill feed and the feed will trip at the set depth (automatic feed will trip within .010"). Do not engage quill feed over 3000 RPM. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: If your milling machine has an R-8 spindle (manufactured on/after Jan 1, 1983):

- Place mounting ring “B” underneath the top of guard “D”.
- Place the two socket head cap screws “A” through the holes in the ring and hand-start them into the threaded holes in the nose cap until hand tight.
- Align the guard square with the table (or at the desired angle).
- Tighten the screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench.
- (If your machine was made before Jan 1, 1983: manually tap the existing spanner-wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap first; do NOT drill new holes or deepen existing holes.) [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

If your milling machine attachment has an Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick-change spindle (manufactured after Jan 1, 1985):

- If the nose cap mounting ring has NOT been installed:
  1. Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button head black finish screw (normally left of the cadmium-finished button head screw) and unscrew the locknut counter-clockwise.
  2. Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (counterbored side of the ring fits against the nose cap).
  3. Lower the quill. Place clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.
  4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.
  5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws to clamp the guard.
  6. Reinstall the quick-change locknut (refer to assembly instructions). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- If the nose cap mounting ring HAS been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6 above and proceed with steps 3–5. For Universal #200 spindles do not remove the quick-change locknut; follow steps 2–5 above (i.e., install guard using existing mounting ring). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Where to attach the guard:
- Attach the guard to the spindle nose cap using the mounting ring and the socket/button head cap screws into the tapped holes in the nose cap (R-8: two threaded holes; Erickson/Universal quick-change: four #8-32 tapped holes in the nose cap). Align the guard square with the table (or as desired) and tighten the clamping screws. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf] [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: You are reversing the spindle direction when you select the low (back-gear) range because the motor reversing switch must be set to reverse when the attachment is in back gear. The manual states: “When the attachment is in direct drive (HIGH SPEED), the motor and spindle are turning in a clockwise direction as viewed from the top of machine. When the attachment is in ‘Back Gear’ (LOW SPEED), the spindle will run backwards (counter‑clockwise) unless the motor direction is reversed by moving switch to ‘Low’.” Also: “The back gear lever is marked Hi‑Lo. This will indicate the proper switch position. They should be positioned alike or the spindle will run backwards. — NOTE — Spindle should run in clockwise position.” [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Additional notes from the manual that may apply:
- Do not change range while the spindle is running — change range only when spindle is stationary. [005__L1__Table_of_Contents__pp13-16_part01.pdf; 007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- If gears don’t mesh when shifting hi/lo, don’t force the lever; rotate spindle by hand to align gears before moving lever. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Key pre‑operation requirements and checks:

- Only authorized/trained personnel may operate the machine; consult a qualified instructor for first‑time operation. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Verify the machine is in good working order and proper maintenance has been performed. Report unusual heat, noise, smoke, or vibration and do not operate if these occur. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Wear required PPE (approved industrial safety glasses with side shields and safety shoes); do not wear gloves, long sleeves, rings, watches, jewelry, loose hair, neckties, etc. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Remove loose parts and tools from the machine/work area and remove chuck wrenches before starting the machine. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Ensure point‑of‑operation safeguarding is installed and suitable; do not rely solely on the general shield if it’s not appropriate for the operation. Inspect guards and safety windows; replace damaged windows and inspect door interlocks for fit and function. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf] [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]

- Verify door interlocks function (e.g., with machine in run mode, close door, run spindle at low speed and confirm door cannot be opened). Inspect safety glass and replace if damaged or >7 years old. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- For tool/quill checks: ensure spindle brake is released before starting motor and that drawbar/collet are secured; do not start machine with cutter in contact with the workpiece; remove gloves and secure hands before changing tools—stop spindle completely first. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf] [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Ensure workpiece is securely clamped and located, use stop blocks as needed, and keep clamps clear of cutter path. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: How should I clean the bridgeport mill when I first receive it?
STUDENT ANSWER: Thoroughly clean the protective coating from the machine with a suitable cleaning solution; do NOT use gasoline or any other flammable cleaning agent. After initial cleaning, do not move the table, saddle, knee, or any movable part until all ways have been well cleaned and lubricated. Then:

- Move table, saddle and knee in one direction by hand to limit stop and clean/lubricate exposed ways.
- Move each unit to the opposite limit stop and clean/lubricate; repeat moving to the opposite stop once more and clean/lubricate.
- Loosen bolts to unlock the ram, move it forward and backward full length to clean and lubricate.

Also note the lubrication recommendations (way surfaces and lead screws: Sunoco Waylube #1180 or equivalent). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Short answer:
Mount the spindle guard to the nose cap area of the spindle using the nose cap mounting ring and the mounting screws, following the sequence for your spindle type. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Steps ( Erickson #30 or Universal #200 spindle)
- If the nose cap mounting ring has not been installed:
  1) Remove the spindle locknut to access the nose cap, then set the ring aside.
  2) Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (ring’s counterbored side against the nose cap).
  3) Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.
  4) Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring into the clamping ring.
  5) Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws to clamp the guard.
  6) Reinstall the quick change locknut.

- If the nose cap mounting ring has been installed, omit steps 1–2 and 6; proceed with steps 3–5.

Note
- For UNIVERSAL #200, the quick change locknut is not to be removed; follow steps 2, 3, 4, and 5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: To get a lower speed/torque, you must use the back-gear (low) setting correctly.

- Set Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to Lo and ensure the gears mesh. Then switch the drum switch to the low range to engage back gears. If the gears do not mesh, don’t force the lever. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Make sure the spindle is stationary when changing from direct drive to back gear, and vice versa. Do not change range while the spindle is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- After selecting Lo, start the motor and use the low-range speed setting (60–500) as indicated on the Speed Change Handwheel. Note that dial speeds are approximate and can vary with belt wear. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

If the mill still doesn’t move in Lo, verify the back-gear mesh, and that the drum switch is set to the low range. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

lever which allows the user to change the torque of the motor mechanicaly. The speed ranges correspond to where the lever is set.

If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Steps to mount the spindle guard on the mill (based on the General Purpose Safeguard instructions):

- If your machine attachment uses Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick-change spindles and the nose cap mounting ring is not installed:
  - Remove the spindle locknut, install the nose cap mounting ring with the ring “O” facing up, and secure with the four button head cap screws “M” (the ring’s counterbored side fits against the nose cap).
  - Lower the quill, place the clamping ring underneath the guard, then install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring into the clamping ring.
  - Align the guard, tighten the screws to clamp the guard, and reinstall the quick-change locknut. If the nose cap mounting ring has already been installed, omit the first and last steps.
  - References: ERICKSON/UNIVERSAL spindles and guard assembly steps [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- If your Series I machine uses an R-8 spindle (general guard installation for R-8 spindles):
  - Place mounting ring “B” underneath the top of guard “D”.
  - Insert two socket head cap screws through the holes in ring and thread into the two drilled/tapped holes in the nose cap; hand-tighten.
  - Align the guard square with the table (or at your preferred angle) and tighten with a 3/16" Allen wrench.
  - Retrofits: if built before 1983, manually tap the existing spanner wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap, then mount the guard as above.
  - References: General Purpose Safeguard installation for R-8 spindle and retrofit notes [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf] and [008__L1__Chapter_8_M-codes__pp365-386__L2__01__8.1_Introduction__pp365-384_part01.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: Short answer:
In low (back gear) range, you must stop the spindle and mesh the back gears before applying power; then switch to LOW. If it’s not engaging, don’t force it and check gear meshing.

Details:
- To switch from direct drive to back gear (low speed): switch B to OFF (stop spindle), move lever C through neutral to LOW to reverse rotation, then switch B to LOW. The gears must mesh; if they do not, do not force the lever. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Do not shift the hi-lo lever while the motor is running. Ensure the motor is not running when changing ranges; speeds are 60–500 (low) and 500–4200 (high). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- For changing speed within a range, start the spindle and then turn the Speed Change Handwheel; speeds are only approximate and belt wear can cause variation. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

If the low range still won’t engage after following these steps and ensuring proper meshing, consult the note that back gears must mesh correctly and do not force the lever. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the difference between high-low switch on the motor and hi-lo lever on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: - The High-Low Range Switch on the motor is the motor reversing switch; in direct drive (High Speed) the spindle turns clockwise, and in back gear (Low Speed) the spindle runs backwards unless the motor direction is reversed by moving the switch to “Low” [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf].
- The Hi-Neutral-Lo Lever on the mill selects the drive path (direct drive vs back gear) for the spindle and must be aligned in the same range; Neutral allows free spindle rotation and High/Low positions change the gear engagement rather than the motor direction by themselves. QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: - Follow the General Purpose Safeguards installation steps for mounting the guard on a milling machine with an R-8 spindle (Series I). Installation involves mounting ring and guard to the nose cap using provided screws as described in the General Purpose Safeguards section. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- If your machine was manufactured on or after January 1, 1983, the guard is mounted by using two holes drilled/tapped in the spindle nose cap and the mounting ring under the guard as follows:
  1) Place mounting ring underneath the top of the guard.
  2) Insert two socket head cap screws through the guard’s ring holes and start them into the spindle nose cap holes until hand-tight.
  3) Align the guard square with the table and tighten screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- For retrofits on pre-1983 machines, manually tap the existing spindle nose cap holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap (no new holes). Then proceed with the mountingRing-under-guard method as above. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- If your machine uses the Universal #200 or Erickson #30 quick-change spindles, refer to the spindle guard assembly notes in the General Safeguards documentation for any spindle-specific steps. The relevant procedural notes are in the same General Purpose Safeguards section. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: Based on the provided manuals, the M-450 uses a High-Low Range Switch to select back gear (low speed) or direct drive (high speed). When the back-gear (low) is selected, the spindle rotation reverses unless the direction is reversed, and the low speed ranges are generated by the back gears. If the machine “not going in” when Low is selected, ensure the back-gear range is engaged correctly and that the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever and related controls are set properly. Also, do not shift the hi-lo lever while the motor is running, and ensure the spindle is stationary before changing ranges. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: Why are there  2 ranges on the speed change flywheel of the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are 2 ranges becuase this mill comes with Hi-Neutral-Lo
lever which allows the user to change the torque of the motor mechanicaly. The speed ranges correspond to where the lever is set.

Try to avoid shifting the hi-lo lever when the feed worm is engaged.
If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: When should I use the power feed on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: Power Feed is used to automatically feed the quill in.  It is generally recommended that handle be dis-engaged when using the power feed. It may be removed by simply pulling handle off.

Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank “N”, Figure 2.11, engages power feed worm gear.
When lever is in right hand hole, the power feed worm gear is engaged.

The worm gear may be disengaged at any time. do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM.

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: - The general mounting instructions for the spindle guard are described in the General Purpose Safeguards section. Attach the guard by mounting ring and screws to the nose cap area of the spindle, then secure with the clamping ring and guard, aligning parallel to the table. Specifically, place the nose cap mounting ring “O” (or ring “B” in the General Purpose guard diagram) against the quill nose cap, install the four screws, position the guard under the spindle, and tighten. - If you are using the Universal #200 Quick Change spindle, follow the same preceding steps (2, 3, 4, and 5) as for the Erickson setup; do not remove the quick change locknut. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- The installation notes emphasize using the appropriate general purpose safeguard and that a safety shield is supplied with the machine; ensure you stop the spindle completely before changing tools, and wear appropriate PPE during operations. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

force the lever

2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: How do I replace the timing belt of the bridegport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: In the 2J-Head and M-450 documentation, timing belt replacement is described under Maintenance Procedures:
- For the 2J-Head (Chapter 3 - Maintenance): Timing Belt Replacement
  - Remove the motor.
  - Lower the quill to full extent.
  - Remove the two lower cap screws “M” from the speed changer housing.
  - Remove the four cap screws “N”.
  - Remove the top assembly “O”, and tap to clear dowels.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the procedure for the spindle type on your machine; attach the guard to the spindle nose cap using the provided mounting ring and screws.

For machines with R-8 spindle taper:
- Place mounting ring “B” underneath the top of the guard “D”.
- Insert the two socket head cap screws “A” through the ring and hand-start them into the threaded holes in the spindle nose cap.
- Align the guard square to the table (or at the desired angle) and tighten the screws with a 3/16" Allen wrench. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

For machines with Erickson #30 Quick Change or Universal #200 Quick Change spindles (machines made on/after 1/1/1985):
- If the nose cap mounting ring has NOT been installed:
  1. Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button-head screw and unscrewing the locknut counterclockwise.
  2. Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap and install the four button-head cap screws “M” (counterbored side fits against the nose cap).
  3. Lower the quill, place clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q”, and position the guard under the spindle.
  4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.
  5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the clamping screws.
  6. Reinstall the quick change locknut per the assembly instructions.
- If the nose cap mounting ring HAS been installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6; proceed with steps 3–5.
- For Universal #200 spindles do NOT remove the quick change locknut; follow steps 2–5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Safety/reminder: use the general-purpose shield provided for chip/coolant protection and ensure the guard is suitable for the specific operation; follow all safety instructions in the manual. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the lubrication schedule for the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Lubricate the machine a few drops twice daily at the indicated points, using the specified lubricants for each area. Key recommendations:  
- Way surfaces and lead screws: Sunoco Waylube #1180 (or equivalent).  
- Milling head (spindle bearings): SAE 10 or 10W light oil (not required for grease‑packed heads).  
- Power feed: Mobilube No. 46 (to sight level).  
- Shaping attachment: Mobil 600W or equivalent.  
- Motor: none required (motor greased for life of bearings).  
- Grease items (as shown on lubrication plate): grease every six months per the lubrication plate instructions.  
(“Few Drops Twice Daily” and lubrication table) [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: I am boring a hole to accept a press fit bearing with the mill. How can I make sure the bearing can easily go in and stay in place?
STUDENT ANSWER: You should bore the hole to the final diameter with a controlled finishing pass and account for tool nose radius/wear so the produced bore matches the intended press‑fit size; also add a small chamfer to the bore entrance so the bearing inserts easily.

Practical steps:
- Use a radial boring canned cycle (e.g., G245) to perform the bore and a final finishing cut to the target diameter, following the cycle structure shown in the G245 examples [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf].  
- Set the tool nose radius and clear/set the radius wear offset correctly so the control compensates by the correct radius (tool nose compensation affects final diameter); adjust radius wear (not geometry) for small production changes and clear wear when installing a new insert [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf].  
- Verify dimensions on a first article and adjust the radius wear offset as needed before full production (use inspection to confirm the press‑fit tolerance) [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf].  
- Add a small entrance chamfer so the bearing can start into the bore without damage (program a short chamfer/lead‑in as part of the finishing pass); verify fit after the chamfer and final bore are cut [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf, 005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf].

If you need specific code examples or numbers (target diameter minus press interference, chamfer size, finish pass allowances), that cannot be determined from the provided documents.

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: It sounds like the spindle direction and range change procedure is not being followed. In back gear (low range) the spindle will run backwards unless the motor reversing (High‑Low Range) switch is moved to “Low,” and you must stop the spindle before changing range. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Action to correct:
- Stop the spindle (switch B to OFF). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to LOW (rotate the spindle by hand to mesh if needed). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Set the drum/variable speed switch to the low range. Ensure the High‑Low Range switch position and the Hi‑Lo lever agree (both indicate Low). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Warnings:
- Do not shift the hi‑lo lever while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to stop the spindle mid cut for precision on the mill. What kind of brake should I be using?
STUDENT ANSWER: Use the machine’s spindle brake to stop and hold the spindle. The head manual describes a spindle brake operated by a brake lever that you move (pull toward or push away from the operator) and then raise to lock the spindle [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf].

On machines with the optional C‑Axis, the brake is a caliper‑style brake that can be applied/released with M14 (brake on) and M15 (brake off) program codes [008__L1__Chapter_8_M-codes__pp365-386__L2__01__8.1_Introduction__pp365-384_part01.pdf].

Caution: always be certain the spindle brake is released before starting the motor to avoid motor damage [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf].

QUESTION: What is the difference between high-low switch on the motor and hi-lo lever on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The High-Low Range Switch is an electrical/motor reversing switch that selects the motor range (direct drive HIGH or back-gear LOW) and can reverse motor direction; it must match the back-gear setting or the spindle will run backwards. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

The Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever is the mechanical gear/clutch selector used to put the attachment into back gear (Lo), direct drive (Hi) or Neutral for free spindle rotation and gear meshing; it physically engages/disengages the clutch/gears and must be positioned (and meshed by hand rotation) before switching ranges. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Notes/precautions:
- The lever provides a Neutral for setup and must not be shifted while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- To change ranges the procedure uses both: stop the spindle, move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to the desired position, then set the range switch. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: Why are there  2 ranges on the speed change flywheel of the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are 2 ranges becuase this mill comes with Hi-Neutral-Lo
lever which allows the user to change the torque of the motor mechanicaly. The speed ranges correspond to where the lever is set.

Try to avoid shifting the hi-lo lever when the feed worm is engaged.
If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: What is the procedure to change the drawbar on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The manual describes how to tighten or loosen the drawbar but does not provide a step‑by‑step "change drawbar" replacement procedure. To loosen/tighten the drawbar:

- Lock the spindle using the spindle brake (pull toward or push away from the operator until it binds), then raise the quill feed handle to hold it.  
- Use the wrench supplied with the machine to tighten the drawbar by hand with a normal amount of pressure (drawbar thread: 7/16"-20 RH).  
- To loosen, back off the drawbar; if the collet does not open immediately, give the knob on top of the drawbar a slight tap.  
- The spindle has a non‑sticking taper and the collet should release readily. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I change the spindle speed on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Do not change spindle speed while the spindle is stationary — change speed only when the spindle is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

To change speed within a range:
- Start the spindle.
- Turn the Speed Change Handwheel (handwheel “A” in Figure 2.16) to select the required speed. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

To change range (direct drive / back gear):
- Stop the spindle (Switch “B” to OFF).
- Move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever (“C”) through Neutral to the desired Low or High position (for Low, move to LOW; for High, move to HIGH).
- For Low: switch “B” to LOW; for High: rotate the spindle by hand until the clutches engage, then switch “B” to HIGH. 
- Do not change range while the spindle is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I replace the timing belt of the bridegport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Remove the motor, then remove the timing belt assembly as follows (steps from the maintenance chapter). [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

- Motor removal (prerequisite)
  1. Run head to lowest speed.  
  2. Disconnect power.  
  3. Remove three screws “A” and cover “B”.  
  4. Using the two screws “A”, compress spring “C”.  
  5. Rotate the speed changer to highest speed.  
  6. Remove the reversing switch from the belt housing.  
  7. Remove the two securing screws “D”.  
  8. Lift the motor and rest the case on stud “E”.  
  9. Ease the belt over the lower drive disc and remove the motor.  
  (See “Motor Removal”, Figure 3.1–3.2.) [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

- Timing belt replacement
  1. Remove the motor (as above).  
  2. Lower the quill to full extent.  
  3. Remove the two lower cap screws “M” from the speed changer housing.  
  4. Remove the four cap screws “N”.  
  5. Remove the top assembly “O” and tap to clear the dowels.  
  6. Replace the timing belt.  
  (See “Timing Belt Replacement”, Figure 3.4.) [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

If you need torque values, detailed fastener locations, or figures, refer to the illustrated figures and callouts in 008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the procedure for the spindle type on your machine:

For machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles:
- If the nose cap mounting ring has NOT been installed: remove the quick‑change locknut (unscrew after removing long button‑head screw), place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap (counterbore side to the nose cap), install the four button head cap screws “M”, lower the quill, place clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle, install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the mounting ring and thread into the clamping ring, align the guard front parallel to the table and tighten, then reinstall the quick‑change locknut. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- If the nose cap mounting ring HAS been installed: omit the locknut removal/installation steps and follow the steps to place the clamping ring, position the guard, install screws N, align and tighten. For Universal #200 spindles do NOT remove the quick‑change locknut; follow steps 2–5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

For machines with R‑8 spindle taper:
- Place mounting ring “B” underneath top of guard “D”, put two socket head cap screws “A” through the ring and hand‑start into the two threaded nose‑cap holes, align guard square with the table (or as desired), then tighten the screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench. If your machine predates Jan 1, 1983, manually tap the existing spanner wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap (do NOT drill new holes or deepen existing holes) before mounting. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Attachment location summary: the guard mounts to the spindle nose cap using the nose‑cap mounting ring(s) and the tapped holes in the nose cap (two holes for R‑8; four #8‑32 holes in the nose cap for Erickson/Universal). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf] [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?

- Change range only when the spindle is stationary. The correct procedure is: switch the spindle OFF (B to OFF), move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to LOW, then set the range switch to LOW. Do not shift the hi‑lo lever while the motor is running. If gears do not mesh, do not force the lever. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

So check that you followed the procedure exactly (stop spindle first), and set the motor reversing/Range switch to the proper LOW position; if the spindle is rotating the wrong direction or the back gears aren’t meshed, the feed may not engage. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

To shift into LOW (back gear):

- Move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to LOW.  
- Set switch “B” to LOW.

To shift into HIGH (direct drive):
- Switch “B” to OFF to stop the spindle.  
- Move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to HIGH.  
- Rotate the spindle by hand until the clutches engage.  
- Set switch “B” to HIGH.  
(Do not shift the hi‑lo lever while the motor is running.) [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to change the depth through knob "I" on the left side of the spindle. How deep should I go if I am boring a 1 inch hole with the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided documents do not specify a required “boring depth” for a 1.00" hole, so the exact depth cannot be determined from the supplied manuals.

Relevant controls and limitations from the manual you should use when setting depth:
- The micrometer nut reads directly in .001" graduations and is used for setting depths (each graduation = .001"). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- The feed control lever (knob “I”) engages the auto quill feed; the quill will automatically trip out at a depth within .010" (.25 mm). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Quill feed rates available are .0015", .003", and .006" per revolution (selectable with the Quill Feed Selector). Do not engage auto quill feed above 3000 RPM. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

If you intend the final bore diameter to be 1.000", set the micrometer nut to move the quill the required amount (e.g., 1.000" from your start/reference point), account for the quill trip tolerance (~±.010"), and choose an appropriate feed rate and spindle speed per the manual’s cautions. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Do not operate the machine until you have read and understood the operator and safety manuals. Then, before operation:

- Verify you (and any operators) are authorized and trained to operate the machine. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Read and understand all machine and control key signs and warning/instruction tags; do not remove them. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Wear required PPE: approved industrial safety glasses with side shields and safety shoes; use respirator/helmet/ear protection when necessary. Do not wear gloves, long sleeves, rings, watches, jewelry, neckties, or have long hair uncontained. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Confirm the machine is in good working order and proper maintenance has been performed; do not operate if unusual or excessive heat, noise, smoke, or vibration is present. Report any damage. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Remove loose parts and tools from the machine and work area; remove chuck wrenches before starting. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Verify guards and point-of-operation safeguarding are installed and appropriate for the operation (the general-purpose shield may not be suitable for all tasks). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Ensure workpiece is securely clamped and stop blocks used where necessary; keep clamps clear of cutter path. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Check electrical and door/safety interlocks are functioning; do not operate with doors open or interlocks defective. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Verify cutters/tools are correct, undamaged, and not in contact with the workpiece before starting; stop spindle completely before changing tools, loading/unloading workpieces, making adjustments, or measuring. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Confirm adequate lighting and that the work area is clean and dry (remove chips, oil, obstacles). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

If any required check cannot be completed or a condition is unsafe, do not operate the machine. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: How do I replace the timing belt of the bridegport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Remove the motor first, then access the speed changer and swap the timing belt, following the manual’s procedure. Key steps (from 008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf):

1. Run head to lowest speed and disconnect power; remove motor per “Motor Removal” procedure. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]  
2. Lower the quill fully. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]  
3. Remove the two lower cap screws “M” from the speed changer housing. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]  
4. Remove the four cap screws “N”. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]  
5. Remove the top assembly “O” (tap to clear dowels). [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]  
6. Replace the timing belt. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]  
7. Reassemble in reverse order and reinstall the motor. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

If uncertain about any fastener or figure references, consult the same document’s Motor Removal and Timing Belt Replacement illustrations before proceeding. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the procedure for the spindle type on your machine and mount the guard to the spindle nose cap or to the nose cap mounting ring as described:

For R-8 spindles (machines manufactured on/after Jan 1, 1983):
- Place mounting ring “B” underneath the top of guard “D”.
- Insert the two socket head cap screws “A” through the ring and hand-start into the two threaded holes in the spindle nose cap until hand tight.
- Align the guard square with the machine table (or at desired angle).
- Tighten the screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

For retrofits on R-8 spindles (machines made before Jan 1, 1983):
- Manually tap the existing spanner-wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap (do not drill new holes or deepen existing ones).
- Then mount the guard as above. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

For machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles (manufactured after Jan 1, 1985) when the nose cap mounting ring is not already installed:
1. Remove the spindle locknut by first removing the long button-head black screw (left of the cadmium-finished button-head screw) and unscrewing the locknut counter-clockwise.  
2. Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap (counterbored side fits against the nose cap) and install the four button-head cap screws “M”.  
3. Lower the quill; place clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.  
4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread into the clamping ring.  
5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the clamping screws.  
6. Reinstall the quick-change locknut (refer to assembly instructions). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

If the nose cap mounting ring is already installed on an Erickson #30 or Universal #200 spindle, omit steps 1, 2, and 6 and proceed with steps to position the clamping ring, install screws N, align and tighten. For Universal #200 quick change spindles do not remove the quick-change locknut; follow steps 2–5 instead. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Where to attach:
- Attach the guard to the threaded holes in the spindle nose cap (R-8) or to the nose cap mounting ring/clamping ring at the quill nose cap for Erickson #30 / Universal #200 spindles; align the guard front parallel to the front of the table unless an angular mounting is desired. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf] [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- Power feed oil: fill to sight level with Mobilube No. 46 S.A.E. 140. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Shaping attachment: Mobil 600W oil or equivalent. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

Note: The lubrication instruction plate (on the machine) gives locations and specific six‑month grease intervals. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: When you switch to low (back gear) range the spindle rotation reverses direction unless you also reverse the motor direction with the High‑Low Range switch. If the Hi–Lo lever and the High‑Low Range switch are not positioned alike the spindle will run backwards. [008__L1__Chapter_2_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf] [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Supporting points:
- The High‑Low Range Switch is a motor reversing switch; in direct drive (HIGH) the spindle turns clockwise, in back gear (LOW) the spindle will run counter‑clockwise unless the motor direction is reversed by moving the switch to “Low.” [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]  
- The back gear lever is marked Hi‑Lo and they should be positioned alike; otherwise the spindle will run backwards. [005__L1__Table_of_Contents__pp13-16_part01.pdf]

To change from direct (High) to back gear (Low):
- Switch “B” to OFF (stop spindle rotation).  
- Move lever “C” through Neutral to LOW (this reverses spindle rotation).  
- Switch “B” to LOW. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

To change from back gear (Low) to direct drive (High):
- Switch “B” to OFF (stop spindle rotation).  
- Move lever “C” through Neutral to HIGH.  
- Rotate the spindle by hand until the clutches are felt to engage.  
- Switch “B” to HIGH. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Additional cautions:
- Do not shift the hi-lo lever while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]  
- Try to avoid shifting the hi-lo lever when the feed worm is engaged. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided documents do not contain a distinct, labeled "pre-operational safety check" checklist for the Bridgeport (M‑450) mill. However, the Safety Recommendations and WARNINGS list several pre‑operation checks and actions you must perform before operating the machine, including:

- Read and understand the operator and safety maintenance manuals and all machine/control key signs. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Do not operate the machine for the first time without a qualified instructor; consult a supervisor if in doubt. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Ensure proper maintenance has been regularly performed and the equipment is in good working order. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Remove any loose parts or tools from the machine and work area (check especially after maintenance). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Remove chuck wrenches before starting the machine. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Verify no unusual or excessive heat, noise, smoke, or vibration — report any such conditions or damaged parts. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Wear required PPE (safety glasses with side shields and safety shoes); use respirator, helmet, ear protection when necessary. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Do not wear gloves, long sleeves, long hair, rings, watches, jewelry, neckties, or other loose items while operating. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Safeguard the cutting zone (point of operation); use the provided general purpose shield or alternate safeguards if required. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Stop the spindle completely before changing tools, loading/unloading workpieces, taking measurements, opening safeguards/covers, or adjusting tooling/workpieces/coolant hoses. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Securely clamp and locate the workpiece; remove objects that could fly loose and use stop blocks where necessary. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

These items together form the essential pre‑operation checks/actions recommended in the manual. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: How do I remove the nose piece of the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided sources do not explicitly describe “removing the nose piece” of the spindle/nose cap as a single procedure. However, related instructions in the manual include:

- To remove the nose cap you must first remove set screw “R” before unscrewing the nose cap “S”; do not attempt to remove the nose cap before removing set screw “R” (Collet Aligning Screw Replacement). Also note a caution not to overtighten when reinstalling. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

- For machines with R-8 spindle taper, the nose cap has two untapped spanner-wrench holes used to remove the nose cap; when retrofitting older machines those holes may be bottom-tapped .250”-20 but you must not drill new holes or deepen existing holes (General Purpose Safeguards / Installation for Machines with R-8 Spindle Taper). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I change the spindle speed on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: To change spindle speed within the current range:
- Start the spindle, then turn the Speed Change Handwheel (P) to select the required speed. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

To change between low (back gear) and high (direct drive) ranges:
- Stop the spindle (switch B to OFF).
- Move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (C) through Neutral to the desired position (LOW for back gear or HIGH for direct drive). Rotate the spindle by hand until gears/clutches mesh.
- Set the drum switch to the corresponding range (LOW or HIGH). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Safety/CAUTIONS:
- Do not change range while the spindle is running; change range only when the spindle is stationary. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Do not change speed when the spindle is stationary; change speed only when the spindle is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: How can I change the e-head speed of the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: 1. Disconnect power from the head. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

2. Loosen the two motor locknuts. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

3. Slide the motor forward. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

4. Reposition the vee belt on the appropriate pulleys for the desired speed. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

5. Slide the motor rearward to tension the vee belt. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

6. Tighten the two motor locknuts. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

(See also: changing speed via moving belt and re-tensioning as shown in Figures and the E-head speed change steps.)
