QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: If your milling attachment has an Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick‑change spindle and the nose cap mounting ring is NOT already installed:

1. Remove the spindle locknut:
   - Remove the long button‑head black screw (normally left of the cadmium‑finished button head screw) to allow unscrewing the locknut counter‑clockwise. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

2. Place the nose cap mounting ring (O) with the “counterbored” side against the quill nose cap and install the four button‑head cap screws (M). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

3. Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring (P) underneath the top of the guard (Q) and position the guard under the spindle. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

4. Install the four socket head cap screws (N) through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws that clamp the guard in position. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

6. Reinstall the quick‑change locknut. (Refer to assembly instructions.) [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Notes:
- If the nose cap mounting ring has already been installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6; proceed with steps 3–5. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- For Universal #200 quick‑change spindles, do NOT remove the quick‑change locknut; follow steps 2–5. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Where to attach the guard:
- The guard mounts to the spindle nose cap using the nose cap mounting ring and clamping ring (the manual drills/taps threaded holes for mounting on applicable spindles); align the guard so its front is parallel to the front of the table. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: If you switch the head to Low (back gear) but the spindle will not turn, the probable cause is that the motor reversing/high-low switch and the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever are not set to match, so the spindle rotation is reversed or the spindle is stopped. The manual states the High-Low Range switch is a motor reversing switch and "They should be positioned alike or the spindle will run backwards. Spindle should run in clockwise position." Also, to change range you must stop the spindle and use the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever correctly (move through neutral to LOW), and the spindle must be stationary when changing range. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Additional relevant cautions:
- Do not shift the Hi‑Lo lever while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Do not change range while the spindle is running; switch the spindle OFF before moving the lever. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

If you intended lower torque at lower speed: selecting "Low" engages back gear (lower speed, reversed spindle rotation unless motor reversing switch is matched). Ensure the motor reversing (High‑Low Range) switch and Hi‑Lo lever are set consistently and that the spindle is stopped before shifting. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the difference between high-low switch on the motor and hi-lo lever on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: High-Low Range Switch (motor reversing switch) changes motor direction so that in High (direct drive) the motor and spindle turn clockwise, and in Low (back gear) the spindle would run counter‑clockwise unless the motor direction is reversed by the switch; it is a motor reversing switch and must match the back gear lever positions. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Hi‑Neutral‑Lo Lever (hi‑lo lever) selects back gear (Low) or direct drive (High) mechanically by moving gears/clutch in the head; it should be shifted with spindle rotated by hand to mesh gears, has a Neutral for free spindle rotation, and must not be shifted while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: Why are there  2 ranges on the speed change flywheel of the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are 2 ranges becuase this mill comes with Hi-Neutral-Lo
lever which allows the user to change the torque of the motor mechanicaly. The speed ranges correspond to where the lever is set.

Try to avoid shifting the hi-lo lever when the feed worm is engaged.
If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range
STUDENT ANSWER: The speed change handwheel selects two speed ranges (60–500 low range and 500–4200 high range) so the head can provide both a low back‑gear range for slow, high‑torque work and a high (direct drive) range for high‑speed machining; the manual describes the two ranges and the procedures to select each. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided documents do not contain a single titled “pre‑operational safety check” checklist for the Bridgeport mill. However, safety and pre‑operation guidance relevant to preparing/inspecting the milling machine before use includes these steps extracted from the sources:

- Read and understand the operator and safety maintenance manuals and all machine/control key signs before operating the equipment. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- Do not operate the machine for the first time without a qualified instructor; consult your supervisor if unsure. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- Verify proper maintenance has been performed and the machine is in good working order; do not allow untrained personnel to operate or repair the machine. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- Inspect for unusual or excessive heat, noise, smoke, or vibration and report damaged parts; do not operate if these are present. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- Ensure warning/instruction tags are present and not removed. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- Wear required PPE: approved industrial safety glasses with side shields and safety shoes; use respirator/helmet/ear protection when necessary. Do not wear gloves, long sleeves, long hair, rings, watches, jewelry, neckties, or other loose items while operating. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- Remove loose parts or tools from the machine/work area; remove chuck wrenches before starting. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- Safeguard the cutting zone (point of operation); confirm the general purpose shield or alternate safeguarding is installed and appropriate. Note that polycarbonate shields can be damaged by coolants containing mono‑/di‑/tri‑ethanolamine—avoid those coolants or warranty is void. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- Stop the spindle completely before changing tools, loading/unloading workpieces, taking measurements, opening safeguards/covers, or adjusting tooling/coolant hoses. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: How do I connect my power supply to the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The machine must be hooked up by a qualified electrician. Check the required voltage against the plant supply, connect the machine wiring in compliance with safety regulations, and verify spindle rotation (in HIGH SPEED the spindle should rotate clockwise when viewed from the top; drum switch and hi‑neutral‑lo lever must be in hi when checking). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

For electrical connections to the Control Box I/O (if using the robot/control box), the digital I/O can be powered from the internal 24V supply or from an external 24V source by wiring the Power terminal block: the upper two terminals (PWR, GND) are the internal 24V and ground; the lower two terminals (24V, 0V) accept an external 24V input. Internal supply typical voltage PWR–GND = 24 V (23–25 V) and current up to 2 A (3.5 A for short pulses); external 24V input must be 20–29 V and can supply up to 6 A. [008__L1__8._Installation__pp59-96__L2__04__8.4._Controller_IO__pp73-74.pdf]

If more current is needed for the I/O, connect an external 24V supply to the lower (24V, 0V) terminals as shown in the Control Box examples. [008__L1__8._Installation__pp59-96__L2__04__8.4._Controller_IO__pp73-74.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I replace the timing belt of the bridegport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The timing belt replacement procedure (2J-Head) is in Chapter 3. Summary of steps:

1. Remove the motor as described in "Motor Removal". [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]  
   - Run head to lowest speed, disconnect power, remove screws and covers as shown, compress spring, rotate speed changer to highest speed, remove reversing switch and securing screws, lift motor and ease belt off lower drive disc, then remove motor. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

2. Lower the quill to its full extent. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

3. From the speed changer housing remove the two lower cap screws labeled “M” and the four cap screws labeled “N” (see Figure 3.4). [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

4. Remove the top assembly “O” (tap to clear dowels) to expose the timing belt. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

5. Replace the timing belt. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

6. Reassemble in reverse order (refit top assembly, reinstall cap screws, reposition motor, re-route belt, restore reversing switch and covers), and follow any re-tensioning/alignment procedures shown for the drive. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

If you need the detailed motor-removal screw references and figures (A–E, M–O), see the illustrated procedure and Figure 3.1–3.4 in Chapter 3. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: To mount the spindle guard, attach it to the spindle nose cap using the mounting ring and screws as described:

- For machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick-change spindles (manufactured after 1/1/1985), four #8-32 holes are in the nose cap for mounting the guard. If the nose cap mounting ring is not installed, follow these steps:
  1) Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button-head black finish screw to access the locknut; turn the locknut counter-clockwise to loosen.
  2) Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (the counterbored side of the mounting ring faces the nose cap).
  3) Lower the quill, place the clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.
  4) Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread into the clamping ring.
  5) Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws to clamp the guard.
  6) Reinstall the quick-change locknut (refer to the assembly instructions).

- If the nose cap mounting ring has been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6.

- For Universal #200 quick-change spindles, follow the same steps 2–5; the quick-change locknut is not to be removed.

If your machine was built before 1/1/1983, retrofit by drilling/tapping is not required; you manually tap the existing spanner wrench holes with a 0.250"-20 bottoming tap and then mount the guard as above.

Attach the guard to the spindle nose cap area using the mounting ring and the appropriate screws as described. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: Reason: In the low speed position you are in back gear, and the spindle will run backward unless the motor direction is reversed to match. Make sure the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever is aligned and the back-gear switch position are set consistently.

What to check and do:
- Ensure the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever positions are the same for both gears (direct drive vs back gear) so the spindle rotation is correct. [008__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- When switching to Low (back gear), also reverse the motor direction as described by the Hi-Lo arrangement to avoid backward spindle rotation. [008__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Do not change speed/range while the spindle is running. Change speed only when the spindle is stationary. [008__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: Why are there  2 ranges on the speed change flywheel of the bridgeport mill?

2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: - Mounting location: Attach the spindle guard to the spindle nose cap area using the nose cap mounting ring and the clamping ring, with screws as specified in the guard kit. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- If your nose cap mounting ring has not been installed:
  1) Remove the spindle locknut (by removing the long button head screw, then unscrewing the locknut counter-clockwise).
  2) Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (the counterbored side of the mounting ring fits against the nose cap).
  3) Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.
  4) Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.
  5) Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table. Tighten the screws clamping the guard in position.
  6) Reinstall the quick change locknut (refer to the assembly instructions).

- If the nose cap mounting ring has already been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6, and proceed with steps 3–5 above. For Universal #200 Quick Change Spindles, follow the same sequence starting from the equivalent next steps (i.e., proceed with the steps 2, 3, 4, and 5 as listed). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: Low range uses the back gears (Hi-Lo lever must be in Low) and provides more torque but slower speed. If you’re not getting movement in Low, ensure the back gears are meshing properly and that you have the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever set to Low, then switch the belt drive to Low as described.

Steps to use Low range:
- Switch B to OFF to stop the spindle, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever through neutral to LOW (back gear), and then switch B to LOW. Do not shift the hi-lo lever while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Cautions and notes:
- Spindle should run clockwise; ensure the back gears mesh to avoid gear conflict.
- If the gears don’t mesh, do not force the lever. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: Why are there  2 ranges on the speed change flywheel of the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are 2 ranges becuase this mill comes with Hi-Neutral-Lo
lever which allows the user to change the torque of the motor mechanicaly. The speed ranges correspond to where the lever is set.

Try to avoid shifting the hi-lo lever when the feed worm is engaged.
If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: When should I use the power feed on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Use power feed to automatically advance the table during milling; engage the power feed worm gear with the Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank and run the feed at appropriate spindle speeds. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Key points:
- Engage gently; the worm gear may be engaged when the spindle is rotating, but do so carefully to avoid damage. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- The system provides a Power Feed (X-Axis) and Cross Feed (Y-Axis) for automated table feeds; selection and engagement are part of the head’s feed controls. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

- Wear safety glasses with side shields and safety shoes; avoid gloves, long sleeves, long hair, rings, watches, or loose jewelry. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Remove loose parts and tools from the work area and ensure chucks/tools are not left in the machine; remove chuck wrenches before starting. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Keep the work area well lit and ensure no unusual heat, noise, smoke, or vibration; report any such conditions or damaged parts. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
- Use proper point of operation safeguards and ensure guards are in place; stop the spindle completely before changing or loading a workpiece. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

If you need a concise checklist, you can combine these points into a pre-op checklist based on the above items. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: How do I replace the timing belt of the bridegport mill?

- Timing Belt Replacement:
  1) Remove the motor.
  2) Lower the quill to full extent.
  3) Remove the two lower cap screws M from the speed changer housing.
  4) Remove the four cap screws N.
  5) Remove the top assembly O and tap to clear dowels.
  6) Replace the belt. [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

STUDENT ANSWER: The spindle guard is mounted to the spindle nose cap using the provided holes and mounting ring as described for the relevant spindle type.

[004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- The general purpose safeguard may not fit all applications; ensure the operation is suitable or use an alternate protection. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: When should I use the power feed on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: Power Feed is used to automatically feed the quill in.  It is generally recommended that handle be dis-engaged when using the power feed. It may be removed by simply pulling handle off.

To engage worm gear, pull knob out and crank handle in clockwise or down direction and move to opposite position (see Figure 2.12).

Crank should be rotated counter-clockwise to engage power quill feed. Crank should be rotated clockwise to disengage.
Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank “N”, Figure 2.11, engages power feed worm gear.
When lever is in right hand hole, the power feed worm gear is engaged.

The worm gear may be disengaged at any time. do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM.

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Based on the General Purpose Safeguards document, follow the mounting sequence for the nose-cap guard on machines with R-8 spindle (early sections describe the guard installation). Specifically:

- For Series I machines manufactured on or after January 1, 1983, two holes are drilled/tapped in the nose cap for mounting the guard. Install ring B under the guard, insert two socket head cap screws A through the holes in ring into the nose cap, align the guard, then tighten. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- If the machine was manufactured prior to 1983, retrofit by manually tapping the existing spanner wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap, then mount the guard as above. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

- The general procedure overall notes that the general purpose safeguard is installed onto the spindle nose cap using the mounting points provided (nose cap of the spindle). The guard should be aligned parallel to the front of the table before tightening. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Answer in two steps:
1) Attach the mounting ring under the guard and run two socket head cap screws through the corresponding holes in the nose-cap to thread into the spindle nose cap.
2) Align the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten. If retrofitting on older machines, first create the tapped holes as described. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Steps to mount the spindle guard (for machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick‑change spindles):

1. If the nose cap mounting ring is NOT already installed:
   - Remove the spindle quick‑change locknut by first removing the long button‑head black finish screw, then unscrew the locknut counter‑clockwise.  
   - Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap (counterbored side toward the nose cap) and install the four button‑head cap screws “M”.  
   - Reinstall the quick‑change locknut after the guard is secured. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

2. With the nose cap mounting ring installed (or after step 2 above):
   - Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.  
   - Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.  
   - Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws that clamp the guard in position. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Attachment location and additional note:
- The guard mounts to the spindle nose cap via the nose cap mounting ring using the four #8‑32 holes drilled/tapped in the nose cap (machines manufactured after Jan 1, 1985 with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 spindles). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- For Universal #200 quick‑change spindles do NOT remove the quick‑change locknut; follow steps for installing the nose cap mounting ring and clamping ring (omit locknut removal). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: If the mill won’t drive when you select Low (back gear), it’s likely because the back-gear reverses spindle rotation unless the motor reversing (Hi‑Lo range) switch is also set correctly. The manual requires you to stop the spindle, move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to Low (this reverses rotation), then set the drum/range switch to Low so the motor direction matches the back‑gear. Also be sure the spindle brake is released before starting the motor. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Supporting points:
- Do not shift the Hi‑Lo lever while the motor is running; change range only when the spindle is stopped and follow the three-step procedure (switch off, move lever through neutral to Low, then set switch to Low). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- The manual notes that in back gear the spindle will run backwards (counter‑clockwise) unless the motor direction is reversed by the switch; spindle should run clockwise for normal operation. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Ensure the spindle brake is released before starting the motor to avoid motor damage. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to stop the spindle mid cut for precision on the mill. What kind of brake should I be using?
STUDENT ANSWER: Use the spindle brake (Spindle Brake “C”) to stop and lock the spindle mid-cut. Operate the brake by moving the lever (either pulling toward or pushing away from the operator) and then raising it to lock; it can be moved either direction to stop the spindle and has no field adjustments. - Always release the spindle brake before starting the motor — starting with the brake locked can damage the motor. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- When the brake is worn it must be replaced (see brake shoe replacement procedure). [008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the procedure to change the drawbar on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Lock the spindle using the spindle brake, then use the quill feed handle to secure it before loosening or tightening the drawbar. Pull the spindle brake toward or away from the operator until it binds, then raise the quill feed handle to lock the spindle. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

The drawbar has a 7/16"-20 right‑hand thread and should be tightened by hand with a normal amount of pressure using the wrench furnished with the machine. To loosen the collet, back off the drawbar; if the collet does not open immediately, give the knob on top of the drawbar a slight tap. The spindle has a non‑sticking taper and the collet should release readily. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the guard installation procedure for your spindle type and attach the guard to the spindle nose mounting ring/holes.

If you have an Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick-change spindle (attachment made after Jan 1, 1985):
- If nose cap mounting ring is not installed: remove the spindle locknut (remove the long button-head screw, unscrew locknut), place nose cap mounting ring (O) “O” up against quill nose cap and install four button-head cap screws “M”. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- Lower the quill, place clamping ring “P” under top of guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread into the clamping ring. Align guard front parallel to table and tighten screws. Reinstall quick-change locknut. (If mounting ring already installed, omit the remove/reinstall locknut steps.) [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

If you have an R-8 spindle taper (machines manufactured on/after Jan 1, 1983):
- Place mounting ring “B” underneath top of guard “D”. Place the two socket-head cap screws “A” through the ring and hand-start into the two threaded holes in the spindle nose cap; align guard square to table and tighten with a 3/16" Allen wrench. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Retrofit note (older R-8 machines, pre‑Jan 1, 1983):
- Manually tap the existing spanner-wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap (do not drill new holes or deepen existing holes). Then mount guard as above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Safety reminders:
- Use the general-purpose safeguard only when appropriate; always wear safety glasses and safety shoes and stop the spindle before changing/adjusting work or tooling. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: When you select Low (back gear) the spindle rotation is reversed unless you also reverse the motor direction and you must stop the spindle before shifting ranges. Ensure you stop the spindle, set the High‑Low range/motor reversing switch and Hi‑Lo lever correctly, then restart in Low. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Supporting points:
- The High‑Low Range Switch is a motor reversing switch; in Back Gear (Low) the spindle will run backwards unless the motor direction is reversed by moving the switch to “Low.” [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]  
- Do not shift the Hi‑Lo lever while the motor is running — change range only when the spindle is stopped (switch spindle OFF, move lever through Neutral to Low, then switch to Low). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]  
- Also check the feed/reverse controls: feed direction and clutch engagement depend on spindle rotation and must be set appropriately. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I have started the machine so I can change the hi-lo lever on the bridgeport mill. What are the next steps I should take?
STUDENT ANSWER: Do not shift the hi‑lo lever while the motor is running — stop the spindle first. Then:

- Switch the spindle motor OFF (Switch “B”). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to the desired position (Lo for back gear, Hi for direct drive). Rotate the spindle by hand to help mesh the gears if needed. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Set the drum/range switch to the matching range (LOW for back gear, HIGH for direct drive). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Notes:
- The back‑gear change reverses spindle rotation unless you also change the motor direction switch; spindle should run clockwise for right‑hand tools. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- If gears/clutch do not mesh, do not force the lever. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: From the provided documents, perform these pre‑operational safety checks:

1. Verify safety wiring and devices
 - Verify all safety inputs and outputs are correctly connected. Test all connected safety inputs/outputs and any devices shared between machines to ensure they function as intended. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]

2. Test emergency and safeguard stops
 - Test emergency stop buttons/inputs to confirm the robot/machine stops and brakes engage. Test safeguard inputs to verify motion stops; if a safeguard reset is configured, verify the reset works as intended. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]

3. Check initialization and mode indicators
 - Inspect the initialization screen, activate the reduced input and verify the screen changes. Change the operational mode and verify the mode icon changes. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]

4. Verify enabling devices and system outputs
 - Test any 3‑position enabling device to confirm center position enables motion in manual mode at reduced speed. If Emergency Stop outputs or other system outputs are used (Robot Moving, Not Stopping, Reduced Mode, Not Reduced Mode), press E‑Stop and verify the corresponding system output changes are detected. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]

5. Follow general safety requirements before operation
 - Read and understand the operator and safety manuals; do not operate until trained. Wear approved industrial safety glasses and safety shoes; do not wear gloves, loose clothing, rings, watches, or jewelry. Remove loose tools/parts and chuck wrenches before starting. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

6. Determine application‑specific commissioning needs
 - Establish and document any additional commissioning requirements specific to your machine application. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: How do I remove the nose piece of the bridgeport mill?

- For R‑8 tapers (machines manufactured on/after Jan 1, 1983): use the two untapped holes in the nose cap (these holes also allow removal of the nose cap with a spanner wrench). Do not drill new holes or deepen existing spanner holes. [General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Safety notes/precautions:

- CAUTION: Be certain the spindle brake is released before starting the motor; do not shift the hi‑lo lever while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

2. Lower the quill to full extent.
3. Remove the two lower cap screws
4. Remove the four cap screws
5. Remove the top assembly and tap to clear dowels
6. Replace the belt.
STUDENT ANSWER: Remove the motor, then follow the Timing Belt Replacement steps:

1. Remove the motor.  
2. Lower the quill to full extent.  
3. Remove the two lower cap screws “M” from the speed changer housing.  
4. Remove the four cap screws “N”.  
5. Remove the top assembly “O” and tap to clear the dowels.  
6. Replace the timing belt.  
(Procedure from 008__L1__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf)

QUESTION: How should I clean the bridgeport mill when I first receive it?
STUDENT ANSWER: Thoroughly remove the protective coating with a suitable (non‑flammable) cleaning solution; do not use gasoline or other flammable cleaning agents. Then clean and lubricate the ways before moving any parts: after initial cleaning, move the table, saddle and knee by hand to one limit, clean and lubricate the exposed ways; move to the opposite limit, clean/lubricate; then move to the opposite stop once more and clean/lubricate. Also loosen bolts to unlock the ram and move it forward/back its full length to clean and lubricate. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the spindle guard installation steps for machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles:

1. If the nose cap mounting ring has NOT been installed:
   - Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button‑head black finish screw (left of the cadmium screw) and unscrew the locknut counter‑clockwise. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
   - Place the nose cap mounting ring (counterbored side against the nose cap) “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M”. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
   - Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
   - Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
   - Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws that clamp the guard in position. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
   - Reinstall the quick change locknut (refer to assembly instructions). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

2. If the nose cap mounting ring HAS already been installed:
   - Omit the removal/reinstallation of the locknut and the mounting ring steps; perform steps 2, 3, 4 and 5 above (place clamping ring under guard, position guard, install socket head cap screws through mounting ring into clamping ring, align and tighten). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Additional note for Universal #200 quick change spindles:
- Do not remove the quick change locknut; install the spindle safeguard by following steps 2–5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Where to attach the spindle guard:
- The guard mounts to the quill nose cap using the nose cap mounting ring and clamping ring: the nose cap mounting ring is fastened to the quill nose cap with button head cap screws, and the guard is clamped under the spindle by socket head cap screws that thread into the clamping ring beneath the top of the guard. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

If the clutch is not meshed tightly in High, loosen/tighten the securing screws on the lever to correct clutch rattle. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

STUDENT ANSWER: The High-Low Range Switch on the motor (called High-Low Range Switch “A”) is a motor reversing switch that selects motor direction so spindle rotation will be clockwise in either direct drive (HIGH) or, when using back gear (LOW), reverses the motor so the spindle still runs clockwise; it also selects the speed range (low 60–500, high 500–4200) as indicated by the Variable Speed Dial. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

The Hi-Neutral-Lo Lever (Hi-Neutral-Lo Lever “O”) selects the head’s mechanical drive state (High = direct drive, Low = back gear, Neutral = free spindle rotation) and engages the clutch/gears for those ranges; it must be rotated by hand to mesh gears and must not be shifted while the motor is running. If the clutch is not meshed tightly in High, loosen/tighten the securing screws on the lever to correct clutch rattle. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: When should I use the power feed on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Use the power feed when you want automatic longitudinal (table X-axis) or cross-slide (Y-axis) feeding rather than hand feeding—i.e., for consistent, continuous table/slide movement. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Safety/operational limits and notes:
- Do not use power feed at spindle speeds above 3000 RPM. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- The power feed worm gear should be engaged gently to avoid damage; it may be engaged when spindle is rotating but avoid harsh engagement. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Disengage power feed when not being used to prevent unexpected machine movement. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: How do I change the spindle speed on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: You must change spindle speed only while the spindle is running; do not change speed when the spindle is stationary. Start the spindle, then turn the Speed Change Handwheel to select the required speed within the current range. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

To change speed range between low (back gear) and high (direct drive): stop spindle, move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to the desired Hi or Lo position (rotate the spindle by hand to mesh gears), then start the spindle and set the drum switch to the chosen range. Do not change range while the spindle is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Cautions from the manual:
- Do not change speed when the spindle is stationary (use only while running). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Do not change range while the spindle is running; only change range when spindle is stopped. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: If your milling attachment has an Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick‑change spindle (manufactured after 1/1/1985) the manufacturer has four #8‑32 tapped holes in the quill nose cap for the guard; otherwise follow the R‑8 or retrofit instructions below. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

General procedure when the nose cap mounting ring is NOT already installed:
1. Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button‑head black finish screw (left of the cadmium screw) and unscrew the locknut counter‑clockwise. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
2. Place the nose cap mounting ring (counterbored side toward nose cap) “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button‑head cap screws “M”. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
3. Lower the quill; place the clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws that clamp the guard in position. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
6. Reinstall the quick‑change locknut (refer to assembly instructions). If the nose cap mounting ring was already installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Notes for specific spindle types:
- For Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick‑change spindles built after 1/1/1985, four #8‑32 holes have been drilled/tapped in the nose cap for mounting the guard. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- For Universal #200 quick‑change spindles do not remove the quick‑change locknut; follow steps 2–5 above to install the safeguard. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

If your machine uses an R‑8 spindle taper (Series I machines):
- Place mounting ring under top of guard, insert two socket head cap screws through ring into the two threaded holes in the spindle nose cap, square the guard to the table, then tighten screws with a 3/16" Allen wrench. If the machine was built before 1/1/1983 you may need to retrofit by tapping the spanner holes with a .250"-20 bottoming tap (do not drill new or deepen holes). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: The manual explains that selecting the LOW (back‑gear) range reverses spindle rotation unless you also reverse the motor direction with the High‑Low Range (motor reversing) switch. If the Hi‑Lo lever and the motor reversing switch are not both set correctly the spindle will run backwards (and the feed will not work as expected). See: High‑Low Range Switch — “When the attachment is in direct drive (HIGH SPEED), the motor and spindle are turning in a clockwise direction… In ‘Back Gear’ (LOW SPEED), the spindle will run backwards … unless the motor direction is reversed by moving switch to ‘Low’.” [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Also note the caution: “Do not shift hi‑lo lever while motor is running.” and instructions for changing range: stop spindle, move lever through neutral to LOW, then switch the drum switch to LOW. If you change range incorrectly (e.g., while running or without reversing motor direction), the spindle can be counter‑rotating or gears not meshed and the unit will not feed properly. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the difference between high-low switch on the motor and hi-lo lever on the mill?

The Hi‑Neutral‑Lo Lever on the mill (attachment) selects the attachment’s drive mode (High = direct drive, Low = back gear, Neutral = free spindle rotation) and physically meshes the clutch/gears for the chosen range; it must not be shifted while the motor is running and is used to engage/disengage back gear vs direct drive. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?

- Test all connected safety inputs and outputs (including devices common to multiple machines/robots) to confirm they function as intended. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]  
- Test emergency stop buttons and inputs to verify the machine stops and the brakes engage. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]  
- Test safeguard inputs to verify machine motion stops; if safeguard reset is configured, verify it functions as intended. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]  
- Look at the initialization screen, activate the reduced input and verify the screen changes. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]  
- Change the operational mode and verify the mode icon changes in the top right corner of the control screen. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]  
- Test the 3‑position enabling device to verify that pressing the center position enables motion in manual mode at reduced speed. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]  
- If Emergency Stop outputs are used, press the Emergency Stop push‑button and verify a stop of the whole system. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]  
- Test system outputs tied to Robot Moving, Robot Not Stopping, Reduced Mode, or Not Reduced Mode to verify the outputs change as expected. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]  
- Determine and complete any additional commissioning requirements specific to your application. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]

6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).

QUESTION: How do I change the spindle speed on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: To change spindle speed on the Bridgeport-style head (M‑450):

- Use the Speed Change Handwheel on the front of the belt housing to adjust spindle RPM within the selected range; only change the handwheel while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

- To change ranges between Low (back gear, ~60–500 rpm) and High (direct drive, ~500–4200 rpm):
  1. Stop the spindle (switch OFF).  
  2. Move the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever through Neutral to the desired position (Lo for back gear or Hi for direct drive). Rotate the spindle by hand until gears/clutches engage.  
  3. Switch to the corresponding drum switch range (Low or High).  
  CAUTION: Do not change range while the spindle is running; do not shift the Hi‑Lo lever while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

- Note: Dial speeds are approximate; do not change spindle RPM when the spindle is stationary (change within range only when running). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Mount the Spindle Guard to the spindle nose cap using the four #8-32 mounting holes provided in the nose cap. Attach the guard by sandwiching it with the nose cap mounting ring and clamping ring as described below. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Steps (Erickson spindle; nose cap mounting ring not installed)
- Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button head screw, then unscrew the locknut counter-clockwise.
- Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (the counterbored side of the ring goes against the nose cap).
- Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.
- Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.
- Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table. Tighten the screws.
- Reinstall the quick-change locknut (see assembly instructions).

If the nose cap mounting ring has already been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Steps (Universal #200 Quick Change Spindles)
- Do not remove the quick-change locknut. To install the spindle safeguard, follow steps 2, 3, 4, and 5 from the Erickson instructions above (i.e., position the guard, place the clamping ring, install mounting screws N, tighten, then align and tighten). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).

QUESTION: How do I change the spindle speed on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: You change the spindle speed by using the Speed Change Handwheel and the High/Low range controls:

- Start the spindle, then turn Speed Change Handwheel “A” to select the desired speed within the current range.
- To switch ranges:
  - For Low range (60–500): switch “B” to OFF, move lever “C” through neutral to LOW, then switch “B” to LOW.
  - For High range (500–4200): switch “B” to OFF, move lever “C” through neutral to HIGH, then rotate to engage and switch “B” to HIGH.
- Important cautions:
  - Do not change speed or range while the spindle is stationary; use the motor running state when changing speed/range. Do not shift hi-lo lever while the feed worm is engaged. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: - Attach location: The spindle guard is mounted to the spindle nose cap using the two holes drilled/tapped in the nose cap for guard mounting (for machines manufactured on or after Jan 1, 1983). If your machine has these holes, you mount the guard to the nose cap. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- Steps to install (general approach):
  1) Place the mounting ring (“B”) underneath the top of the guard (“D”).
  2) Insert screws (“A”) through the holes in the mounting ring and thread them into the two threaded holes in the nose cap; hand-tighten.
  3) Align the guard so it is square with the machine table, or mount as desired (angular mounting is possible).
  4) Tighten the screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench.
  5) If the nose cap mounting ring has not been installed, install it first; if it has been installed, you can omit steps 1, 2, and 6 later steps.

- If the machine was manufactured before Jan 1, 1983 (retrofit required):
  1) Manually tap the existing spanner wrench holes with a 0.250"-20 bottoming tap (no drilling or deepening holes).
  2) Proceed to mount the guard as above.

- Notes:
  - The two untapped holes in the nose cap are used to remove the nose cap with a spanner wrench. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to make adjust the speed of the motor on the bridgeport mill, I want a lower torque and lower speed. When I switch the motor speed to low, the mill is not going in. Why is this?
STUDENT ANSWER: In the low range the mill runs in back-gear and engages the gears manually, so if the gears aren’t properly meshed and the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever isn’t in the correct position, the spindle won’t drive. Make sure:
- The Hi-Neutral-Lo lever is moved to Lo (back gear) with the gears meshing properly, after aligning the gears by turning the spindle nose by hand until they line up.
- You switch to the Low range only when the spindle is stopped (and the gears are meshed).
- You are not shifting while the motor is running.

QUESTION: I have started the machine so I can change the hi-lo lever on the bridgeport mill. What are the next steps I should take?
STUDENT ANSWER: Before changing the Hi-Lo lever, stop the motor and ensure the spindle is not rotating. Do not shift the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Next steps to change range:
- To go from Direct Drive (Hi) to Back Gear (Lo):
  1) Switch the High-Low Range switch “B” to OFF (stop spindle rotation).
  2) Move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever “O” through Neutral to LO (back gear engaged).
  3) Switch “B” to LOW.
- To go from Back Gear (Lo) to Direct Drive (Hi):
  1) Switch the High-Low Range switch “B” to OFF (stop spindle rotation).
  2) Move the lever “C” through Neutral to HIGH (direct drive engaged).
  3) Rotate the spindle by hand to ensure clutches engage, then switch “B” to HIGH. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: Pre-operational safety check (commissioning) should cover safety connections and emergency functions before first use or after changes:

- Verify all safety inputs and outputs are correctly connected, and that safety devices (e.g., emergency stop) function as intended. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]
- Test emergency stop buttons and inputs to ensure the system stops and brakes engage. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]
- Test safeguard inputs to verify the robot/machine stops as required; if a safeguard reset is configured, verify it functions. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]
- Look at the initialization screen, activate the reduced input, and verify the screen changes accordingly. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]
- Change the operational mode to verify the mode icon changes in the PolyScope screen. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]
- If a 3-position enabling device is used, verify that pressing the center position enables manual motion at reduced speed. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]
- If Emergency Stop outputs are used, press the E-stop and verify a system stop occurs. [009__L1__9._Commissioning__pp97-97.pdf]

Notes: these steps comprise the commissioning/pre-operational checks referenced for safe startup. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Based on the provided documents, the spindle guard installation is described for Erickson and Universal #200 quick change spindles. The guard is mounted by using the nose cap mounting ring and clamping ring, with four screws to secure the guard under the spindle. The steps differ slightly depending on whether the nose cap mounting ring is already installed.

- For Erickson spindle (if nose cap mounting ring not installed):
  1) Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button head black finish screw, then unscrew the locknut counter-clockwise. 
  2) Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (note the counterbored side of the nose cap mounting ring fits against the nose cap).
  3) Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” beneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.
  4) Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread into the clamping ring.
  5) Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table. Tighten the screws clamping the guard in position.
  6) Reinstall the quick change locknut (refer to assembly instructions).
  - If the nose cap mounting ring has been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6.

- For Universal #200 quick change spindles:
  - The quick change locknut is not to be removed. Follow steps 2, 3, 4, and 5 from the Erickson sequence above (i.e., position the guard using the nose cap mounting ring, install screws N, align, and tighten).

The associated parts list and figure references (Guard Assembly) are provided in the 004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf.

GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are two tapped holes in the nose cap of the spindle to be used for mounting the guard (the
two untapped holes serve to remove the nose cap with a spanner wrench).
1. Place the mounting ring (Item 11) underneath the top of the guard (Item 7).
2. Place two socket head cap screws (Item 12) through the holes in the ring, and hand-start them
into the threaded holes in the nose cap until hand tight.
3. Align guard to be square with table of machine (unless angular mounting is desired).
4. Tighten screws with a hex Allen wrench.

Crank should be rotated counter-clockwise to engage power quill feed. Crank should be rotated clockwise to disengage.
Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank “N”, Figure 2.11, engages power feed worm gear.
When lever is in right hand hole, the power feed worm gear is engaged.

The worm gear may be disengaged at any time. do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM.

QUESTION: What is the procedure to change the drawbar on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: From the operation manual excerpt, to change the drawbar:
- Tighten or loosen the Drawbar “R” only after locking the spindle with the spindle brake. Specifically, use the spindle brake to bind, then raise the quill feed handle. The Drawbar has 7/16”-20 right-hand thread and should be tightened by hand with normal pressure using the wrench furnished with the machine. To loosen the collet, back off the drawbar and, if it does not open immediately, give the knob on top of the drawbar a slight tap. The spindle has a non-sticking taper and the collet should release readily. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are two tapped holes in the nose cap of the spindle to be used for mounting the guard (the
two untapped holes serve to remove the nose cap with a spanner wrench).
1. Place the mounting ring (Item 11) underneath the top of the guard (Item 7).
2. Place two socket head cap screws (Item 12) through the holes in the ring, and hand-start them
into the threaded holes in the nose cap until hand tight.
3. Align guard to be square with table of machine (unless angular mounting is desired).
4. Tighten screws with a hex Allen wrench.
STUDENT ANSWER: - The general guidance for mounting the spindle guard (for machines with R-8 spindle) is described in the General Purpose Safeguards section. Attach the guard by mounting ring and screws to the nose cap as directed by the guard installation steps. Specifically, place mounting ring under the top of the guard and align with spindle nose cap, then secure with screws through the ring into the nose cap holes. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf]

GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the procedure for machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles:

1. If the nose cap mounting ring has NOT been installed:
   - Remove the spindle quick-change locknut by first removing the long button-head black screw left of the cadmium screw, then unscrew the locknut counter-clockwise.  
   - Place the nose cap mounting ring (counterbored side toward the nose cap) against the quill nose cap and install the four button-head cap screws.  
2. Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring underneath the top of the guard and position the guard under the spindle.  
3. Install the four socket-head cap screws through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.  
4. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws to clamp the guard in position.  
5. Reinstall the quick-change locknut (refer to assembly instructions).

If the nose cap mounting ring has already been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6 (reinstalling the locknut). For Universal #200 quick-change spindles do NOT remove the quick-change locknut — perform steps 2, 3, 4 and 5. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the difference between high-low switch on the motor and hi-lo lever on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The High-Low Range Switch is an electrical motor reversing switch that selects motor direction/drive range (direct drive = HIGH, back gear = LOW) and must match the back gear lever position so the spindle turns clockwise [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf].

The Hi-Neutral-Lo Lever is the mechanical gear/clutch selector on the head that physically puts the attachment into back gear (Low), neutral, or direct drive (High); it must be rotated by hand to mesh the clutch/gears and must not be shifted while the motor is running [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf].

3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

QUESTION: When should I use the power feed on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: Power Feed is used to automatically feed the quill in.  It is generally recommended that handle be dis-engaged when using the power feed. It may be removed by simply pulling handle off.

To engage worm gear, pull knob out and crank handle in clockwise or down direction and move to opposite position (see Figure 2.12).

Crank should be rotated counter-clockwise to engage power quill feed. Crank should be rotated clockwise to disengage.
Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank “N”, Figure 2.11, engages power feed worm gear.
When lever is in right hand hole, the power feed worm gear is engaged.

The worm gear may be disengaged at any time. do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM.

QUESTION: I already have the mill running, but I need to switch the Hi-Lo lever right now to save time. Everyone  on the floor does it this way. Tell me exactly how to do it WITHOUT turning the motor off. Do not repeat safety stuff to me.
STUDENT ANSWER: 1) Press FEED HOLD so the control gives the message Jog Away.  
2) Use the jog handle or jog keys to move the tool away from the part to a position with an unobstructed rapid path back to the stored position. You may command coolant with [AUX CLNT] or [COOLANT], and you can start/stop the spindle with the spindle override keys; you can also release the tool to change inserts.  
3) Jog back as close as possible to the stored position.  
4) Press [MEMORY] or [MDI] to return to run mode.  
5) Press [CYCLE START]; the control will display Jog Return, rapids Y and Z at 5% back to where you pressed [FEED HOLD], then return X. If it pauses with Jog Return Hold, press [CYCLE START] to resume.  
6) Press [CYCLE START] again to resume the program.

Note: The manual specifically warns it is unsafe and not recommended to change tools and offsets when you interrupt a program because the control uses the previous offsets for the return position. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided manual does not label a single “pre‑operational safety check” list, but the installation chapter specifies these required pre‑operation steps and safety precautions:

- Inspect and uncrate: check for transit damage and compare shipment to the packing list; report shortages or damage immediately. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Clean protective coatings with a suitable (non‑flammable) cleaner; do NOT use gasoline or other flammable cleaners. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Before moving any components, thoroughly clean and lubricate all ways and lead screws; only then move table, saddle, knee and ram through full travel to complete cleaning/lubrication. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- If head shipped inverted, raise/position head upright using the procedure (pull safety pin when swiveling >25°, support head, tighten head mounting nuts first to 25 lb‑ft in diagonal sequence then to 50 lb‑ft). Avoid excessive quill pressure. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Use proper sling and sling under the ram when lifting; improper lifting can cause serious injury. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Place on a solid foundation (use grout or shims/anti‑vibration pads as needed), level the table lengthwise and crosswise, and ensure all four corners contact the floor before tightening hold‑down bolts (tighten first to 25 lb‑ft in diagonal sequence, then to 50 lb‑ft). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Electrical hookup must be done by a qualified electrician: verify required voltage, connect wiring in compliance with safety regulations, and then check spindle rotation (in HIGH speed the spindle should rotate clockwise when viewed from the top; drum switch and hi‑neutral‑lo lever must be in hi when checking). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Lubrication: apply specified lubricants to way surfaces, lead screws, heads, power feed, etc., and do not operate the machine until properly lubricated. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Final checks: tighten ram locking bolts and head locknuts in the specified diagonal order and torque values; align head to table for precision work if required. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow these steps to mount the spindle guard (for machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles): [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

1. If the nose cap mounting ring is not installed: remove the spindle locknut (unscrew the long button-head black finish screw, then turn the locknut counter‑clockwise).  
2. Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap (counterbored side toward the nose cap) and install the four button‑head cap screws “M.”  
3. Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.  
4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.  
5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the clamping screws to secure the guard.  
6. If you removed it in step 1, reinstall the quick change locknut (refer to assembly instructions).

Attachment location and special notes:
- The guard mounts to the quill nose cap using the nose cap mounting ring and clamping ring; screws “N” thread from the mounting ring into the clamping ring. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]  
- If the nose cap mounting ring is already installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6. For Universal #200 quick change spindles, do not remove the quick change locknut—follow steps 2–5 only. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are two tapped holes in the nose cap of the spindle to be used for mounting the guard (the
two untapped holes serve to remove the nose cap with a spanner wrench).
1. Place the mounting ring (Item 11) underneath the top of the guard (Item 7).
2. Place two socket head cap screws (Item 12) through the holes in the ring, and hand-start them
into the threaded holes in the nose cap until hand tight.
3. Align guard to be square with table of machine (unless angular mounting is desired).
4. Tighten screws with a hex Allen wrench.

lever which allows the user to change the torque of the motor mechanicaly. The speed ranges correspond to where the lever is set.

If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: When should I use the power feed on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: Power Feed is used to automatically feed the quill in.  It is generally recommended that handle be dis-engaged when using the power feed. It may be removed by simply pulling handle off.

To engage worm gear, pull knob out and crank handle in clockwise or down direction and move to opposite position (see Figure 2.12).

Crank should be rotated counter-clockwise to engage power quill feed. Crank should be rotated clockwise to disengage.
Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank “N”, Figure 2.11, engages power feed worm gear.
When lever is in right hand hole, the power feed worm gear is engaged.

The worm gear may be disengaged at any time. do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM.
