QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided installation chapter does not present a single labelled “pre‑operational safety check,” but the manual gives these required pre‑operation steps and safety precautions:

- Uncrate and inspect for transit damage; report any damage to the representative and carrier. Check shipment against the packing list for shortages. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Clean protective coating from the machine with a suitable cleaning solution (do NOT use gasoline or other flammable cleaning agents). Do not move table, saddle, knee, or any movable part until all ways have been well cleaned and lubricated. Follow the manual’s stepwise cleaning and lubrication of ways and ram. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Reinstall/position controls and head:
  - Reverse hand cranks (remove retaining lead screw nut and install hand cranks). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
  - If head was shipped upside‑down, raise and align the head upright per instructions (pull safety pin, support head, rotate via swivel bolt, align indicator to ZERO, then tighten mounting nuts in diagonal sequence to 25 lb‑ft then 50 lb‑ft). Avoid excessive pressure on the quill. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Verify machine is properly supported and secured:
  - Use proper sling when lifting (place sling under ram). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
  - Place on solid foundation or use shims/anti‑vibration pads so all four corners contact floor; bolt down and tighten hold‑down bolts in diagonal sequence first to 25 lb‑ft then to 50 lb‑ft. Level table lengthwise and crosswise with a precision instrument. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Electrical and rotation checks (must be done by a qualified electrician):
  - Confirm required voltage matches supply and connect wiring per safety regulations. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
  - Check spindle rotation: in HIGH SPEED range the spindle should rotate clockwise when viewed from the top (drum switch and hi‑neutral‑lo lever must be in hi range when checking). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Lubrication and final tightening:
  - Lubricate per lubrication chart (way surfaces, lead screws, milling head, power feed, etc.). Do not operate until properly lubricated. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
  - Tighten head locknuts and ram locking bolts in the specified diagonal order to the listed torques (head locknuts and three ram locking bolts to 50 lb‑ft where noted). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the spindle-guard installation procedure for mills with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick-change spindles as given in the source. Summary of steps:

1. If the nose cap mounting ring is NOT already installed:
   - Remove the spindle locknut by first removing the long button-head black finish screw (left of the cadmium-finished button-head screw) and then unscrew the locknut counter‑clockwise. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
   - Place the nose cap mounting ring (O) “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button-head cap screws (M). (The counterbored side of the ring fits against the nose cap.) [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

2. With the nose cap ring in place (or if it was already installed, skip step 1 and step 6 below):
   - Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring (P) underneath the top of the guard (Q) and position the guard under the spindle. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
   - Install the four socket-head cap screws (N) through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
   - Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws that clamp the guard in position. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

3. If you removed the quick-change locknut in step 1, reinstall the quick-change locknut per the assembly instructions. If the nose cap mounting ring was already installed, do NOT remove the quick-change locknut—omit steps 1 and 6. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Where to attach the spindle guard:
- The guard attaches to the quill nose cap via the nose cap mounting ring and clamping ring; four #8-32 tapped holes in the nose cap (for quick-change spindles manufactured after Jan 1, 1985) are used to mount the guard assembly. Position the guard so its front is parallel to the front of the table. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Parts and hardware referenced (for identification): see the Quick Change Shield Assembly and R-8 Shield Assembly item lists in the source. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the difference between high-low switch on the motor and hi-lo lever on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The High-Low Range Switch (motor reversing switch) and the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever serve different functions:

- High-Low Range Switch (motor reversing switch): Selects motor/spindle rotation direction appropriate to the attachment’s drive mode; in direct drive (HIGH SPEED) the motor and spindle turn clockwise, while in Back Gear (LOW SPEED) the spindle will run counter-clockwise unless the motor direction is reversed by moving this switch to “Low.” It is a motor reversing control. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

- Hi-Neutral-Lo Lever: Selects the mechanical drive range of the attachment (High/direct drive, Neutral for free spindle rotation, or Low/back gear) and engages the taper clutch or gears; it must be shifted with the spindle hand-rotated to mesh clutch/gears and should not be shifted while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Supporting points:
- The High-Low Range Switch affects motor direction so the spindle rotates correctly in the chosen gear range. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- The Hi-Neutral-Lo lever physically puts the attachment into back gear or direct drive and requires manual hand rotation to mesh; it provides a Neutral for setup/indicating work. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided document does not contain an explicit titled "pre-operational safety check" checklist. However, the Installation chapter gives pre‑operation safety and setup actions you must perform before operating the Bridgeport mill:

- Uncrate and inspect for transit damage; report any damage immediately to the representative and carrier. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Check shipment against the packing list and report shortages to the supplier. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Thoroughly clean protective coating from the machine with a suitable (non‑flammable) cleaning solution. Do NOT use gasoline or other flammable cleaners. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Do not move table, saddle, knee, or any movable part until all ways have been well cleaned and lubricated; then move each unit through its travel while cleaning and lubricating exposed ways (steps 1–5 in Cleaning). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- If machine was shipped with head inverted, position head upright following the described procedure (loosen locknuts, pull safety/stop pin, support head, swivel into vertical, align indicator to ZERO, retighten nuts in diagonal sequence to 25 lb‑ft then 50 lb‑ft). Avoid excessive pressure on the quill. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Reinstall/adjust hand cranks if shipped inverted: engage locks, remove retaining nut, install hand cranks properly. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- When lifting or moving, use proper sling under the ram as illustrated; improper lifting can cause serious injury. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Set machine on a solid, level foundation; use grout, shims, or anti‑vibration pads as required and ensure all four corners contact the floor before tightening hold‑down bolts to avoid twisting the column. Tighten hold‑down bolts in diagonal sequence first to 25 lb‑ft then to 50 lb‑ft. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Level the machine lengthwise and crosswise with a precision instrument. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Have a qualified electrician connect the machine to the plant supply; verify required voltage, make wiring connections per safety regulations, and check spindle rotation (in HIGH SPEED range spindle should rotate clockwise viewed from top; drum switch and hi‑neutral‑lo lever must be in hi range when checking). MACHINE MUST be hooked up by a qualified electrician. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Fully lubricate before operating per the Lubrication chart (way surfaces/lead screws, spindle bearings, power feed, etc.) and follow lubrication plate instructions—do not operate until properly lubricated. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- For precision work, align/square the head to the table using the vertical adjusting worm shaft and indicator, then tighten head locknuts and ram locking bolts (three ram locking bolts to 50 lb‑ft). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the procedure for your spindle type as described in 004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf.

If your milling machine has an Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick‑change spindle and the nose cap mounting ring has NOT been installed:
1. Remove the spindle locknut by first removing the long button‑head black finish screw (left of the cadmium screw) and then unscrew the locknut counter‑clockwise. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
2. Place the nose cap mounting ring (O) “O” side up against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws (M). Note: the counterbored side of the ring fits against the nose cap. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
3. Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring (P) underneath the top of the guard (Q) and position the guard under the spindle. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
4. Install the four socket head cap screws (N) through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws to clamp the guard in position. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
6. Reinstall the quick‑change locknut (refer to assembly instructions). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

If the nose cap mounting ring HAS already been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6; start at step 3. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Where to attach the guard:
- The guard is attached at the quill nose cap using the nose cap mounting ring and clamping ring; the four socket head cap screws (N) pass through the nose cap mounting ring and thread into the clamping ring to secure the guard beneath the spindle. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: Why are there  2 ranges on the speed change flywheel of the bridgeport mill?

If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided document does not contain an explicit titled "pre-operational safety check" checklist. However, the installation chapter lists preparatory and safety-related steps you should perform before operating the milling machine, including:

- Uncrating: remove protective crating/skids carefully and report any transit damage to the representative and carrier. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Check shortages: verify shipment against the itemized packing list and report missing parts immediately. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Cleaning and lubrication before moving parts:
  - Thoroughly clean protective coating with a suitable (non‑flammable) cleaning solution; do NOT use gasoline or other flammable cleaners.  
  - Do not move table, saddle, knee, or any movable part until all ways have been well cleaned and lubricated.  
  - Follow the sequence given: move each unit to limit stops while cleaning/lubricating exposed ways; loosen bolts to unlock the ram and move it full length to clean/lubricate. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Position and secure the head (if delivered inverted):
  - Support head while rotating upright, withdraw/replace safety pin as instructed, align indicator to ZERO, and tighten head mounting nuts first to 25 lb‑ft (diagonal sequence) then to 50 lb‑ft; avoid excessive pressure to prevent quill distortion. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Handling/lifting safety: use a proper sling placed under the ram when lifting; improper lifting could cause serious injury. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Foundation and securing:
  - Place on solid, level foundation; use grout/shims or anti‑vibration pads as needed.  
  - Ensure all four corners contact the floor before tightening hold‑down bolts to avoid twisting the column and binding the ways.  
  - Tighten hold‑down bolts in diagonal sequence first to 25 lb‑ft, then to 50 lb‑ft. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Leveling: level the work table lengthwise and crosswise with a precision instrument. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Electrical hookup: machine must be hooked up by a qualified electrician; verify required voltage, connect wiring in compliance with safety regulations, and check spindle rotation (in high speed the spindle should rotate clockwise when viewed from top; drum switch and hi‑neutral‑lo lever must be in hi range when checking). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Lubrication: ensure all required lubrication is applied before operating (way surfaces, lead screws, head/spindle bearings, power feed, etc., per lubrication table); do not operate until properly lubricated. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

- Final head alignment and tightening: for precision work, adjust and square the head using the vertical adjusting worm shaft and indicator; then tighten head locknuts in diagonal order and ram locking bolts to 50 lb‑ft. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: To mount the Spindle Guard, follow these steps (for Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles):

- If the nose cap mounting ring has not been installed:
  1) Remove the spindle locknut by unscrewing the locknut counter-clockwise after removing the long button head black finish screw.
  2) Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (the counterbored side of the ring goes against the nose cap).
  3) Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.
  4) Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread into the clamping ring.
  5) Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table. Tighten the screws clamping the guard in position.
  6) Reinstall the quick change locknut. (If the nose cap mounting ring has been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6.)

- If the nose cap mounting ring has been installed:
  - Omit steps 1, 2, and 6; perform steps 3, 4, and 5 as listed above.

Notes:
- For Universal #200 quick change spindles, the quick change locknut is not to be removed; use steps 2, 3, 4, and 5.

QUESTION: Why are there  2 ranges on the speed change flywheel of the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are 2 ranges becuase this mill comes with Hi-Neutral-Lo
lever which allows the user to change the torque of the motor mechanicaly. The speed ranges correspond to where the lever is set.

Try to avoid shifting the hi-lo lever when the feed worm is engaged.
If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Steps to mount the Spindle Guard (for Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles):

- If the nose cap mounting ring has not been installed:
  1) Remove the spindle locknut by loosening the locknut with the long button head screw, then turn the locknut counter-clockwise to remove. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
  2) Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (the counterbored side of the ring fits against the nose cap). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- Position the guard:
  3) Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
  4) Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
  5) Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table. Tighten the screws clamping the guard in position. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- Reinstall the spindle hardware:
  6) Reinstall the quick change locknut. Refer to assembly instructions. If the nose cap mounting ring has been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Notes:
- For Universal #200 QUICK CHANGE SPINDLES, the quick change locknut is not to be removed; follow steps 2, 3, 4, and 5 to install the safeguard. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Where to attach:
- The guard is positioned under the spindle and secured with the mounting ring and clamping ring, with the front of the guard aligned parallel to the table front. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

force the lever

2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

force the lever

1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.

QUESTION: When should I use the power feed on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: Power Feed is used to automatically feed the quill in.  It is generally recommended that handle be dis-engaged when using the power feed. It may be removed by simply pulling handle off.

To engage worm gear, pull knob out and crank handle in clockwise or down direction and move to opposite position (see Figure 2.12).

Crank should be rotated counter-clockwise to engage power quill feed. Crank should be rotated clockwise to disengage.
Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank “N”, Figure 2.11, engages power feed worm gear.
When lever is in right hand hole, the power feed worm gear is engaged.

The worm gear may be disengaged at any time. do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM.

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Where to attach: mount the guard to the spindle nose cap using the nose-cap mounting ring and the tapped holes in the nose cap (two threaded holes for R‑8 taper; four #8‑32 holes for Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick‑change spindles). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf] [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Steps — R‑8 spindle taper (machines manufactured on/after Jan 1, 1983)
- Place mounting ring under the top of the guard.  
- Insert the two socket head cap screws through the ring and hand‑start them into the two threaded holes in the nose cap.  
- Align the guard square with the machine table (or at the desired angle) and tighten the screws with a 3/16" Allen wrench. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Retrofit for pre‑1983 R‑8 machines
- Manually tap the existing spanner‑wrench holes with a .250"‑20 bottoming tap, do not drill new holes or deepen existing holes.  
- Then mount the guard as above. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Steps — Erickson #30 quick‑change or Universal #200 quick‑change spindles (machines manufactured after Jan 1, 1985)
- If nose cap mounting ring is NOT installed:
  1. Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button‑head black finish screw, then unscrew the locknut counter‑clockwise.  
  2. Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M”. (Counterbored side of the ring fits against the nose cap.)  
  3. Lower the quill, place clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.  
  4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.  
  5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the clamping screws.  
  6. Reinstall the quick‑change locknut (refer to assembly instructions). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- If the nose cap mounting ring is already installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- For Universal #200 spindles do NOT remove the quick‑change locknut; follow steps 2–5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Safety reminders
- Use the polycarbonate shield provided and follow all machine safety instructions (wear safety glasses/shoes, stop spindle before changing tools, etc.). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: Why are there  2 ranges on the speed change flywheel of the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are 2 ranges becuase this mill comes with Hi-Neutral-Lo
lever which allows the user to change the torque of the motor mechanicaly. The speed ranges correspond to where the lever is set.

Try to avoid shifting the hi-lo lever when the feed worm is engaged.
If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: From the supplied installation chapter, perform these pre‑operational safety checks before operating the Bridgeport mill: [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

1. Inspect and uncrate
 - Remove protective crating carefully and inspect for transit damage; report any damage immediately.  
 - Check shipment against the packing list and report shortages. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

2. Clean and prepare moving parts
 - Thoroughly clean protective coating with a suitable (non‑flammable) cleaning solution — do NOT use gasoline or other flammable cleaners.  
 - Do NOT move table, saddle, knee, or any movable part until all ways have been well cleaned and lubricated. Follow the prescribed sequence of moving and lubricating each way and the ram. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

3. Mechanical setup and orientation
 - Reinstall or reverse hand cranks as required per shipping configuration.  
 - If the head was shipped inverted, follow the head‑upright procedure: withdraw safety pin, loosen mounting bolts, support the head while swiveling upright, reinsert safety pin after passing 25°, and tighten head mounting nuts first to 25 lb·ft (diagonally) then to 50 lb·ft. Avoid excessive quill pressure. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

4. Foundation, leveling, and securing
 - Place machine on a solid foundation (use grout, shims, or anti‑vibration pads as needed).  
 - Level the table lengthwise and crosswise with a precision instrument.  
 - Ensure all four corners contact the floor before tightening hold‑down bolts; tighten hold‑down and head nuts in the specified diagonal sequence first to 25 lb·ft then to 50 lb·ft to avoid twisting/binding. Secure machine to floor to prevent movement or tipping. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

5. Power and electrical safety
 - Have a qualified electrician connect the machine. Verify required voltage matches plant supply and connect wiring in compliance with safety regulations.  
 - Check correct spindle rotation: in HIGH SPEED range the spindle should rotate clockwise when viewed from the top (drum switch and hi‑neutral‑lo lever must be in hi range when checking). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

6. Lubrication and final checks
 - Lubricate all indicated areas with the recommended lubricants and do not operate the machine until it is properly lubricated (refer to lubrication plate and Figure 1.8). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

If you need the exact torque/bolt locations, lubrication types, or the head‑upright illustrations, refer to the referenced pages in 006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf.

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the procedure for the spindle type on your machine; attach the guard to the spindle nose cap using the provided mounting ring and screws.

For machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick-change spindles:
- If the nose cap mounting ring is not installed:
  1. Remove the spindle locknut by first removing the long button-head black screw, then unscrew the locknut counter‑clockwise.  
  2. Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap (counterbored side against the nose cap) and install the four button-head cap screws “M.”  
  3. Lower the quill, place the clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q,” position the guard under the spindle.  
  4. Install the four socket-head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread into the clamping ring.  
  5. Align the guard front parallel to the table and tighten the clamping screws.  
  6. Reinstall the quick-change locknut.  
- If the nose cap mounting ring is already installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6.  
- Note: For Universal #200 quick‑change spindles the quick-change locknut is not to be removed; follow steps 2–5 only. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

For machines with R‑8 spindle taper:
1. Place mounting ring “B” under the top of guard “D.”  
2. Insert the two socket-head cap screws “A” through the ring and hand-start into the two threaded holes in the nose cap until hand‑tight.  
3. Align the guard square with the machine table (or at desired angle).  
4. Tighten the screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench.  
- Retrofit note: If your machine was made before Jan 1, 1983, manually tap the existing spanner-wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap (do not drill new holes or deepen existing holes), then mount as above. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Attachment location summary: fasten the guard to the spindle nose cap using the nose-cap mounting ring and the threaded holes in the nose cap (two holes for R‑8, four #8-32 holes for Erickson/Universal quick-change spindles). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided documents do not label a single “pre‑operational safety check” procedure, but the Installation chapter lists the preparatory and safety steps to perform before operating the mill. Key steps (as given) are:

- Inspect for transit damage and shortages; report any damage or missing parts immediately. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Remove protective crating carefully and clean protective coating from the machine with a suitable cleaning solution (do NOT use gasoline or other flammable cleaning agents). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Do not move the table, saddle, knee or any movable part until all ways have been thoroughly cleaned and lubricated; then move each unit through its travel while cleaning and lubricating the exposed ways and the ram. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Reinstall or reverse hand cranks (remove retaining lead screw nut and install hand cranks properly) and follow the head‑uprighting procedure if delivered upside‑down (support head, pull safety pin, swivel into vertical, align indicator, tighten head bolts to specified torques in the diagonal sequence: first 25 lb‑ft, then 50 lb‑ft). Avoid excessive quill pressure. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Ensure proper lifting/slinging when moving the machine and observe the ram/table positions shown for lifting. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Set the machine on a solid, level foundation (use grout/shims/anti‑vibration pads as required), confirm all four corners contact the floor before tightening hold‑down bolts, and level the table lengthwise and crosswise with a precision instrument. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Tighten mounting/lock bolts in the specified diagonal sequence and torques to avoid binding (first 25 lb‑ft, then 50 lb‑ft). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Have a qualified electrician connect the machine to the plant supply, verify required voltage compatibility, make connections in compliance with safety regulations, and check spindle rotation (in HIGH SPEED range spindle should rotate clockwise when viewed from top; drum switch and hi‑neutral‑lo must be in hi range). Machine must be hooked up by a qualified electrician. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Do not operate the machine until properly lubricated per the lubrication chart (way surfaces, lead screws, spindle bearings, power feed, etc.). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the procedure that matches your spindle type and manufacture date.

For machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles (manufactured after Jan 1, 1985):
- If the nose cap mounting ring has NOT been installed:
  1. Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button head black finish screw (left of the cadmium-finished button head screw), then unscrew the locknut counter‑clockwise.  
  2. Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” (ring, guard) “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M”. (Counterbored side fits against the nose cap.)  
  3. Lower the quill. Place clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.  
  4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring.  
  5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws clamping the guard.  
  6. Reinstall the quick change locknut (refer to assembly instructions).  
- If the nose cap mounting ring HAS already been installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6 and perform steps 3–5. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

For Universal #200 quick change spindles: do NOT remove the quick change locknut; install the safeguard by following steps 2, 3, 4 and 5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

For machines with R‑8 spindle taper (machines manufactured on or after Jan 1, 1983):
1. Place mounting ring “B” underneath top of guard “D.”  
2. Insert the two socket head cap screws “A” through the holes in the ring and hand‑start them into the threaded holes in the spindle nose cap until hand tight.  
3. Align the guard square with the table (unless an angular mounting is desired).  
4. Tighten the screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench.  
- If the machine was manufactured before Jan 1, 1983, retrofit by bottoming‑tapping the existing spanner wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap (do NOT drill new holes or deepen existing holes), then mount as above. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Where to attach the spindle guard:
- Attach the guard to the spindle nose cap using the nose cap mounting ring and socket/button head cap screws (for Erickson/Universal quick change spindles use the four #8-32 screws into the clamping ring; for R‑8 use the two threaded nose cap holes). Ensure the guard is aligned parallel/square to the table before tightening. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the difference between high-low switch on the motor and hi-lo lever on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: High-Low Range Switch (motor reversing switch)
- The High-Low Range Switch “A” (Figure 2.2) is a motor reversing switch that selects direct drive (HIGH SPEED) or back gear (LOW SPEED); in direct drive the motor and spindle turn clockwise viewed from the top, while in back gear the spindle will run counter‑clockwise unless the motor direction is reversed by the switch. It must be positioned to match the back gear lever or the spindle will run backwards. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Hi‑Neutral‑Lo Lever (gear/clutch range on the mill attachment)
- The Hi‑Neutral‑Lo Lever “O” (Figure 2.13) selects the attachment’s back gear (Low), neutral (free spindle rotation), or direct drive (High) for the spindle/attachment. It mechanically meshes the clutch or gears for high or low range; neutral allows free rotation for setup. The manual warns not to shift the hi‑lo lever while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Summary (difference)
- The High‑Low Range Switch is an electrical motor reversing switch controlling motor rotation/direction. The Hi‑Neutral‑Lo Lever is a mechanical clutch/gear selector on the attachment that engages back gear, neutral, or direct drive and requires manual meshing of gears. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

force the lever

1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank “N”, Figure 2.11, engages power feed worm gear.
When lever is in right hand hole, the power feed worm gear is engaged.

The worm gear may be disengaged at any time. do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM.

Supporting notes from the supplied material that relate to moving head/ram components:
- Do not move the table, saddle, knee, or any movable part until all ways have been well cleaned and lubricated; initial procedure: move table, saddle and knee by hand in one direction to limit stop, clean/lubricate ways, then move to opposite stops and repeat. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- To move the ram during initial cleaning: loosen bolts to unlock the ram, then move it forward and backward the full length to clean and lubricate. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- To position the milling head/ram upright: lower the knee ~6" (150 mm), withdraw safety pin on left side of ram adapter, loosen four unit head mounting bolts, support the head manually and use a spanner on the swivel bolt to wind into upright position, press safety pin back into ram adapter after passing 25°, then tighten bolts. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

If you want a step‑by‑step on operating or jogging the ram slide (not just initial cleaning/positioning), that procedure is not included in the supplied excerpts.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Follow the procedure appropriate to your spindle type as described in the manual excerpts.

For machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles (guard mounting ring not installed):
1. Remove the spindle locknut by removing the long button‑head black finish screw (left of the cadmium button‑head screw) and unscrew the locknut counter‑clockwise. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
2. Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” (counterbored side toward the nose cap) against the quill nose cap and install the four button‑head cap screws “M”. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
3. Lower the quill, place the clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q”, and position the guard under the spindle. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
4. Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
5. Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table and tighten the screws to clamp the guard in position. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
6. Reinstall the quick change locknut (refer to assembly instructions). If the nose cap mounting ring is already installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

For Universal #200 quick change spindles specifically: do not remove the quick change locknut; follow steps 2–5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

For machines with R‑8 spindle taper (manufactured on or after Jan 1, 1983):
1. Place mounting ring “B” underneath the top of guard “D”. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
2. Insert the two socket head cap screws “A” through the ring and hand‑start them into the threaded nose cap holes until hand tight. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
3. Align the guard square to the machine table (unless angular mounting is desired). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]
4. Tighten the screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Retrofit note for R‑8 spindles (machines manufactured before Jan 1, 1983): manually tap the existing spanner wrench holes with a .250”‑20 bottoming tap (do not drill new holes or deepen existing holes), then mount as above. [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

Attachment location: the guard mounts to the spindle nose cap using the nose cap mounting ring (Erickson/Universal) or the mounting ring and the two threaded holes in the R‑8 nose cap; align the guard front parallel to the table when tightening. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the difference between high-low switch on the motor and hi-lo lever on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: High-Low Range Switch (motor reversing switch): It is a motor reversing switch on the attachment that selects direct drive (HIGH SPEED) or back gear (LOW SPEED) and also reverses the motor direction when in LOW so the spindle still runs clockwise; the switch position should match the back gear lever; spindle should run clockwise. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Hi-Neutral-Lo Lever (hi-lo lever on the mill): It is the mechanical gear/clutch selector on the head that puts the attachment into back gear (Low), neutral (free spindle rotation), or direct drive (High); you must rotate the spindle by hand to mesh gears/clutch, and do not shift this lever while the motor is running. If clutch rattle occurs in High, loosen/tighten the lever securing screws to allow the clutch spring to adjust. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

To engage worm gear, pull knob out and crank handle in clockwise or down direction and move to opposite position (see Figure 2.12).

Crank should be rotated counter-clockwise to engage power quill feed. Crank should be rotated clockwise to disengage.
Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank “N”, Figure 2.11, engages power feed worm gear.
When lever is in right hand hole, the power feed worm gear is engaged.

The worm gear may be disengaged at any time. do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM.

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided documents do not contain a labeled “pre-operational safety check” checklist for the Bridgeport (M-450) mill. However, the installation chapter contains several pre‑use safety and setup steps you should perform before operating the machine:

- Uncrate and inspect for transit damage; report damage immediately to the representative and carrier. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Check shipment against the itemized packing list and report shortages immediately. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Clean protective coating from the machine with a suitable cleaning solution (do NOT use gasoline or other flammable cleaning agents). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Do not move table, saddle, knee, or any movable part until all ways have been thoroughly cleaned and lubricated; follow the specified sequence of moving and lubricating ways and ram. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- If delivered with the head inverted, reposition the head upright following the specified detent/swivel and torque procedure; support the head manually while raising and tighten head mounting bolts in the specified diagonal sequence to 25 lb‑ft, then 50 lb‑ft. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Use proper slings when lifting the machine and place sling under ram as illustrated. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Place the machine on a solid, level foundation (concrete preferred); use grout, shims, or anti‑vibration pads as needed, and secure the machine to the floor to prevent movement or tipping. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Level the machine lengthwise and crosswise with a precision instrument before use. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Tighten base and head bolts in the specified diagonal sequence first to 25 lb‑ft then to 50 lb‑ft to avoid quill bind. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Have a qualified electrician connect the machine to the power supply, verify correct voltage and compliance with safety regulations, and check spindle rotation (spindle should rotate clockwise from the top in HIGH speed range; drum switch and hi‑neutral‑lo lever must be in hi range when checking). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]  
- Do not operate the machine until it is properly lubricated according to the lubrication chart (way surfaces, lead screws, milling head bearings, power feed, etc.). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

If you need a concise pre‑operational checklist formatted for shop use, I can produce one based strictly on these steps.

QUESTION: How should I clean the bridgeport mill when I first receive it?
STUDENT ANSWER: Thoroughly clean the protective coating from the machine with a suitable cleaning solution — do not use gasoline or any other flammable cleaning agent. After initial cleaning, do not move the table, saddle, knee, or any movable part until all ways have been well cleaned and lubricated. Then:

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Here is how to mount the spindle guard and where to attach it.

Common mounting location
- The guard is mounted to the nose cap region of the spindle using holes drilled/tapped in the nose cap. For machines with Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles (manufactured after Jan 1, 1985), four #8-32 holes exist in the nose cap for guard mounting. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles (after 1985)
- If the nose cap mounting ring has not been installed:
  1) Remove the spindle locknut by taking out the long button head black finish screw to loosen the locknut; turn the locknut counterclockwise to unscrew.
  2) Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” up against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (the counterbored side of the mounting ring faces the nose cap).
  3) Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle.
  4) Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the mounting ring into the clamping ring.
  5) Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table. Tighten the screws to clamp the guard.
  6) Reinstall the quick change locknut (refer to assembly instructions).
- If the nose cap mounting ring has already been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6.

- For Universal #200 quick change spindles specifically: the quick change locknut is not to be removed. To install the spindle safeguard, follow steps 2, 3, 4, and 5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

General case for R-8 spindle (older or other configurations)
- If your Series I machine (R-8 spindle) has two holes in the nose cap for mounting the guard (manufactured on/after Jan 1, 1983):
  1) Place mounting ring “B” underneath the top of guard “D”.
  2) Place two socket head cap screws “A” through the holes in the ring and hand-start them into the threaded holes in the nose cap until hand-tight.
  3) Align the guard square with the table (adjust if angular mounting is desired).
  4) Tighten screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench.
- If the machine was manufactured before Jan 1, 1983 (retrofit):
  1) Manually tap the existing spanner wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap; do not drill or deepen holes.
  2) Proceed to mount the guard as above.

Where to attach
- Attach via the nose cap mounting holes in the spindle nose cap region using the specified mounting rings and screws, as described for Erickson/Universal spindles or the R-8 nose cap provisions. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: How do I remove the nose piece of the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The nose piece removal involves removing the spindle locknut first, then mounting the guard/nose cap assembly. Follow these steps for Erickson or Universal quick-change spindles:

- Remove the spindle locknut by taking out the long button head black finish screw (located just left of the cadmium-finished button head screw on the locknut). This allows you to unscrew the locknut counter-clockwise. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- If the nose cap mounting ring has not been installed: place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap and install the four button head cap screws “M” (counterbored side of the ring fits against the nose cap). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- Lower the quill. Place the clamping ring “P” underneath the top of the guard “Q” and position the guard under the spindle. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- Install the four socket head cap screws “N” through the nose cap mounting ring and thread them into the clamping ring. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- Align the front of the guard parallel to the front of the table. Tighten the screws to clamp the guard in position. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- Reinstall the quick change locknut (refer to assembly instructions). If the nose cap mounting ring has already been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Note: For UNIVERSAL #200 quick-change spindles, the quick change locknut is not to be removed; follow steps 2–5 to install the safeguard. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I lock the spindle on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: To “lock” the spindle when installing the guard, you temporarily remove the spindle locknut and then reinstall it to lock the spindle.

- Erickson spindle (after Jan 1, 1985): 
  - Remove the spindle locknut by taking out the long button head black finish screw, then unscrew the locknut counter-clockwise.
  - Install the nose cap mounting ring and four screws, position the guard, then install the four socket head cap screws to secure.
  - Reinstall the quick change locknut to lock the spindle. If the nose cap mounting ring is already installed, skip steps 1, 2, and 6. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- Universal #200 quick change spindles: 
  - The quick change locknut is not to be removed; to install the safeguard, follow steps 2, 3, 4, and 5 (mount guard, position, and secure). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: - Attach the spindle guard to the nose cap mounting holes on the spindle. For most Series I milling machines with an R-8 spindle, the manufacturer drilled two holes in the nose cap for mounting the guard.

- Steps (R-8 spindle mounting):
  - Place the mounting ring “B” underneath the top of the guard “D”.
  - Insert two socket head cap screws “A” through the holes in the ring and hand-start them into the threaded holes in the spindle’s nose cap until hand tight.
  - Align the guard so it is square with the table (or as desired for the operation).
  - Tighten the screws with a 3/16” Allen wrench.

- If your machine was manufactured after Jan 1, 1983, these steps apply as the standard mounting method. If your machine was manufactured prior to Jan 1, 1983, retrofits require manually tapping the existing spanner wrench holes with a 0.250”-20 bottoming tap before mounting (do not drill new holes or deepen existing ones).

- If you have Erickson #30 Quick Change or Universal #200 Quick Change Spindles (manufactured after Jan 1, 1985) the spindle nose cap has four #8-32 holes for mounting the guard; follow the guard installation procedure in the manual (see steps in the Erickson/Universal section), noting to omit steps 1, 2, and 6 if the nose cap mounting ring has already been installed.

QUESTION: What are the steps for changing the tool on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: find the proper sized wrench (usually around 3/4") to rotate the
draw bar located above the head of the mill, then have one
hand to push against the spindle brake with 1 hand then use 
the other hand to rotate the wrench against the draw bar to start 
loosening it, once the draw bar starts to feel loose start rotating 
the drawbar with your hand instead of the wrench, once the draw 
bar is loose enough that you can start pulling it out of the head, 
then you can let go of the spindle brake and use that same hand 
to hold the collette and with the other hand to pick up the drawbar 
and dropping it a foot higher than where it originaly started

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: The instructions for mounting the spindle guard (general purpose safeguard) are in the General Purpose Safeguards manuals. Key steps:

- For Series I milling machines manufactured on or after Jan 1, 1983, two holes are drilled and tapped in the nose cap spindle for mounting the guard. Use mounting ring “B” under the top of the guard “D”, insert two socket head cap screws through the holes in ring and hand-start into the threaded holes in the nose cap, align the guard square with the table, then tighten with a 3/16” Allen wrench. Retrofit if the machine is pre-1983 by tapping the existing spanner wrench holes as described, then mount as above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

- For Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles, follow the procedure in the same guard assembly notes: remove nose cap mounting ring if needed, install ring and screws as described, position the guard under the spindle, then reinstall the guard screws and tighten; the exact steps depend on whether the nose cap mounting ring is installed. If the ring is already installed, you omit steps 1, 2, and 6. The guard assembly is shown and includes parts A–Q in the bill of materials. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Where to attach:
- Attach the general purpose safeguard to the spindle nose cap area using the drilled/tapped holes in the nose cap (or retrofit holes if pre-1983), via the mounting ring under the top of the guard and the socket head cap screws as described. Ensure the front of the guard is aligned parallel to the front of the table and tighten securely. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Use mounting ring “B” under the top of the guard “D”, insert two socket head cap screws through the holes in ring and hand-start into the threaded holes in the nose cap, align the guard square with the table, then tighten with a 3/16” Allen wrench. Where to attach:
- Attach the general purpose safeguard to the spindle nose cap area using the drilled/tapped holes in the nose cap (or retrofit holes if pre-1983), via the mounting ring under the top of the guard and the socket head cap screws as described. QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: According to the General Purpose Safeguards (M-450) and the spindle guard assembly notes, mount the guard to the spindle nose cap using the predrilled holes and follow the guided sequence.

Steps to mount and attach the spindle guard:
- For machines with R-8 spindle nose cap:
  - If holes are drilled and tapped (after Jan 1, 1983), place mounting ring under the top of the guard and thread two socket head cap screws through the ring into the spindle nose-cap holes. Align the guard square to the table, then tighten with a 3/16" Allen wrench. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
  - If retrofitting (pre-1983), manually tap the existing spanner wrench holes with a 0.250"-20 bottoming tap, then mount the guard as above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- For Erickson #30 or Universal #200 quick change spindles:
  - Follow the general procedure described in the guard assembly instructions: position the guard, insert the four button head cap screws through the nose cap mounting ring, thread into the clamping ring, align, and tighten. If the nose cap mounting ring has not been installed, complete steps 1–6 as specified; if it has been installed, omit steps 1, 2, and 6. The quick-change locknut is reinstalled after mounting. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Where to attach:
- Attach the guard to the spindle nose cap using the holes provided on the spindle nose cap (the mounting holes are drilled/tapped by the spindle manufacturer for this purpose). Ensure the front of the guard is aligned parallel to the front of the table and tighten to secure. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are 2 ranges becuase this mill comes with Hi-Neutral-Lo
lever which allows the user to change the torque of the motor mechanicaly. The speed ranges correspond to where the lever is set.

If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

QUESTION: When should I use the power feed on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: Power Feed is used to automatically feed the quill in.  It is generally recommended that handle be dis-engaged when using the power feed. It may be removed by simply pulling handle off.

To engage worm gear, pull knob out and crank handle in clockwise or down direction and move to opposite position (see Figure 2.12).

Crank should be rotated counter-clockwise to engage power quill feed. Crank should be rotated clockwise to disengage.
Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank “N”, Figure 2.11, engages power feed worm gear.
When lever is in right hand hole, the power feed worm gear is engaged.

The worm gear may be disengaged at any time. do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM.

QUESTION: There is a small allen key hole on the chuck. What is this for on the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

1. Use felt pen, mark reference line on quill and nose cap “S”, Figure 3.9.  
2. Remove set screw “R”.  
3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.

QUESTION: I am trying to mount the Spindle Guard onto the Mill. What are the steps I should follow? Where do I attach the spindle guard?
STUDENT ANSWER: Where to attach:
- The spindle guard attaches to the spindle nose (nose cap) using a nose-cap mounting ring and clamping ring; screws thread into the tapped holes in the nose cap. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Steps (R-8 spindle machines, manufactured on/after Jan 1, 1983):
1. Place mounting ring “B” underneath the top of guard “D”.
2. Place the two socket-head cap screws through the ring and hand-start them into the threaded holes in the spindle nose cap.
3. Align the guard square with the table (or angular as desired).
4. Tighten the screws with a 3/16" Allen wrench.  
(If machine was made before Jan 1, 1983, manually tap the existing spanner-wrench holes with a .250”-20 bottoming tap first; do not drill new holes or deepen existing holes.) [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Steps (machines with Erickson #30 quick change or Universal #200 quick change spindles):
- If nose cap mounting ring has NOT been installed:
  1. Remove the quick-change locknut by removing the long button-head black screw and unscrewing the locknut counter-clockwise.
  2. Place the nose cap mounting ring “O” against the quill nose cap and install the four button-head cap screws “M”.
  3. Lower the quill, place clamping ring “P” under the top of the guard “Q”, and position the guard under the spindle.
  4. Install the four socket-head cap screws “N” through the nose-cap mounting ring and thread into the clamping ring.
  5. Align the guard front parallel to the table and tighten the clamping screws.
  6. Reinstall the quick-change locknut.  
- If the nose cap mounting ring HAS been installed, omit steps 1, 2 and 6.  
- For Universal #200 quick-change spindles do NOT remove the quick-change locknut; follow steps 2–5 above. [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]

Safety/reminders:
- Use the mounting holes provided in the nose cap; do not drill or deepen holes (spindle damage may result). [004__L1__General_Purpose_Safeguards__pp9-12.pdf]
- The general-purpose shield is polycarbonate; avoid coolants containing mono-/di-/tri-ethanolamine which can degrade the shield. Always follow other safety practices (wear safety glasses, stop spindle before adjusting, etc.). [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the difference between high-low switch on the motor and hi-lo lever on the mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The High‑Low Range Switch is a motor reversing switch (electrical) that changes motor rotation for the selected range, while the Hi‑Neutral‑Lo lever is a mechanical gear/clutch selector that engages either back‑gear (low) or direct‑drive (high) (mechanical). [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

Supporting details:
- High‑Low Range Switch: when the attachment is in direct drive (HIGH) motor and spindle turn clockwise; in back gear (LOW) the spindle would run counter‑clockwise unless the motor direction is reversed by this switch. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]
- Hi‑Neutral‑Lo Lever: used to put the attachment into back gear or direct drive; Neutral permits free spindle rotation and the lever meshes/disengages clutch or gears (rotate spindle by hand to facilitate meshing). Do not shift this lever while the motor is running. [007__L1__Chapter_2_-_Operation__pp27-48.pdf]

QUESTION: Why are there  2 ranges on the speed change flywheel of the bridgeport mill?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: There are 2 ranges becuase this mill comes with Hi-Neutral-Lo
lever which allows the user to change the torque of the motor mechanicaly. The speed ranges correspond to where the lever is set.

Try to avoid shifting the hi-lo lever when the feed worm is engaged.
If the back gears do not mesh, do not
force the lever

To obtain 60 to 500 (low range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Lo” position (back gear).
3. Use the low range on the drum switch to engage the back gears.

To obtain 500 to 4200 (high range):
1. Hold the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever (right rear side of the attachment) so the gears are clear of one another.
2. Rotate the spindle nose by hand until the gears line up, then move the Hi-Neutral-Lo lever to the “Hi” position.
3. Set the drum switch to high range

Power Feed Transmission Engagement Crank “N”, Figure 2.11, engages power feed worm gear.
When lever is in right hand hole, the power feed worm gear is engaged.

The worm gear may be disengaged at any time. do not use power feed at speeds above 3000 RPM.

QUESTION: What are the steps for the pre-operational safety check on the bridgeport mill?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided documents do not contain a single titled “pre‑operational safety check” procedure; however, the installation and initial‑settings sections list pre‑use steps and safety cautions you should perform before operating the Bridgeport mill:

- Uncrate and inspect for transit damage; report any damage or shortages. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Thoroughly remove protective coating and clean the machine (do NOT use gasoline or other flammable cleaners). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Clean and lubricate all exposed ways; do not move table/saddle/knee until they have been cleaned and lubricated. Move each unit through its travel while cleaning/lubricating. Do not operate until properly lubricated. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Unlock and exercise the ram (loosen bolts and move forward/back) to clean/lubricate the ram. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- If delivered with head inverted, raise and secure the head upright per the positioning procedure and tighten head mounting nuts in diagonal sequence to specified torques (25 lb‑ft then 50 lb‑ft). Avoid excessive pressure on the quill. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Verify proper lifting/sling placement and that the machine is secured/leveled on a solid foundation (use grout, shims or anti‑vibration pads); tighten hold‑down bolts only after all four corners contact the floor. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Level the table lengthwise and crosswise with a precision instrument. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Have a qualified electrician connect power; check required voltage, make connections in compliance with safety regulations, and verify correct spindle rotation (spindle should rotate clockwise from top in HIGH speed). [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]
- Follow lubrication recommendations (way lubricant, head oil, power‑feed oil) before operation. [006__L1__Chapter_1_-_Installation__pp17-26.pdf]

GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: That small Allen-head screw you see toward the lower backside of the spindle nose is the used to align the collet.

3. Unscrew nose cap “S”.  
4. Remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”.  
5. Replace “U”; insert collet and check that the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the bottom of the guide slot.  
6. Replace lock screw “T”.  
7. Replace nose cap “S”; check felt pen markings for correct alignment.  
8. Replace set screw “R”. **CAUTION - DO NO OVERTIGHTEN as this will cause distortion.**  
9. Check gap “V” (.003”, .08mm).  


NOTICE
Do not attempt to remove nose cap before removing set screw “R”. Doing so will cause serious damage.
